sentence_analysis.text: Public policy researcher Anthony Fowler studied the history of elections in Australia, a country that requires citizens to vote.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Fowler argues that requiring citizens to vote leads to a significant increase in voters who would otherwise not have the time or motivation to vote.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Thus, election results in countries that require citizens to vote better reflect the preferences of the country as a whole.
sentence_analysis.label: Conclusion

sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: However, forcing people to vote may have negative consequences.
sentence_analysis.label: Contrast

sentence_analysis.text: Shane P. Singh and Jason Roy studied what happens when a country requires its citizens to vote.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: They found that when people feel forced to vote, they tend to spend less time looking for information about their choices when voting.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: As a result, votes from these voters may not reflect their actual preferences.
sentence_analysis.label: Conclusion

sentence_analysis.text: Dance choreographer Alvin Ailey’s deep admiration for jazz music can most clearly be felt in the rhythms and beats his works were set to.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Ailey collaborated with some of the greatest jazz legends, like Charles Mingus, Charlie Parker, and perhaps his favorite, Duke Ellington.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: With his choice of music, Ailey helped bring jazz to life for his audiences.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Jazz is present throughout Ailey’s work, but it’s most visible in Ailey’s approach to choreography.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Ailey often incorporated improvisation, a signature characteristic of jazz music, in his work.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: When managing his dance company, Ailey rarely forced his dancers to an exact set of specific moves.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Instead, he encouraged his dancers to let their own skills and experiences shape their performances, as jazz musicians do.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: Historians studying pre-Inca Peru have looked to ceramic vessels to understand daily life among the Moche people.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: These mold-made sculptures present plants, animals, and human faces in precise ways—vessels representing human faces are so detailed that scholars have interpreted facial markings to represent scars and other skin irregularities.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Some historians have even used these objects to identify potential skin diseases that may have afflicted people at the time.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Art historian and archaeologist Lisa Trever has argued that the interpretation of Moche 'portrait' vessels as hyper-realistic portrayals of identifiable people may inadvertently disregard the creativity of the objects’ creators.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Moche ceramic vessels, Trever argues, are artworks in which sculptors could free their imagination, using realistic objects and people around them as inspiration to explore more abstract concepts.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: Italian painters in the 1500s rarely depicted themselves in their work.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Even more rare were self-portrait paintings that portrayed the artist as a painter.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: At the time, painting was not yet respected as a profession, so painters mostly chose to emphasize other qualities in their self-portraits, like their intellect or social status.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: In the city of Bologna, the first artist to depict themself painting was a man named Annibale Carracci.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: A painting of his from around 1585 shows Carracci in front of an easel holding a palette.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: In their self-portraits, Bolognese artists typically avoided referring to the act of painting until the mid-1600s.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: However, Lavinia Fontana’s 1577 painting, Self-Portrait at the Keyboard, stands out as the earliest example of such a work by an artist from Bologna.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Although the artist is depicted playing music, in the background, one can spot a painting easel by a window.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: Flamingos are known for their vibrant pink coloring, but they’re actually born with gray feathers.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Their pink color comes from eating brine shrimp, but brine shrimp aren’t naturally pink either.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Animals can’t produce carotenoids, the pigments that provide the pink hue.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: The algae that brine shrimp feed on, however, can produce these pigments.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: Thus, the pinker the flamingo, the more shrimp it has eaten.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Ecologist Juan Amat has found that flamingos apply a kind of makeup to make themselves appear pinker.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: A gland near their tail contains pigments that come from the food they eat.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: When the flamingos groom themselves using the pigments, their feathers become pinker.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Flamingos may do this to improve their success during mating season, when they would benefit from looking pinker.
sentence_analysis.label: Conclusion

sentence_analysis.text: Today the starchy root cassava is found in many dishes across West Africa, but its rise to popularity was slow.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Portuguese traders brought cassava from Brazil to the West African coast in the 1500s.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: But at this time, people living in the capitals further inland had little contact with coastal communities.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Thus, cassava remained relatively unknown to most of the region’s inhabitants until the 1800s.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Cassava’s slow adoption into the diet of West Africans is mainly due to the nature of the crop itself.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: If not cooked properly, cassava can be toxic.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: Knowledge of how to properly prepare cassava needed to spread before the food could grow in popularity.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: The arrival of formerly enslaved people from Brazil in the 1800s, who brought their knowledge of cassava and its preparation with them, thus directly fueled the spread of this crop.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: On April 26th, 1777, Sybil Ludington rode 40 miles by horse through Putnam County, New York, to gather up local militia.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: British forces were burning nearby Danbury, Connecticut, and Ludington wanted to rally rebel troops to meet them.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Although she was only 16 years old at the time, her brave feat made Ludington one of the heroes of the American Revolution.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Since then, Ludington has been widely celebrated, inspiring postage stamps, statues, and even children’s TV series.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: Historian Paula D. Hunt researched the life and legacy of Sybil Ludington but found no evidence for her famous ride.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Although many articles and books have been written about Ludington, Hunt believes writers may have been inventing details about Ludington as they retold her story.
sentence_analysis.label: Concession

sentence_analysis.text: Ludington is revered by Americans today, but there simply isn’t a strong historical record of her heroic ride.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: For decades, bluegrass musicians have debated whether their genre should exclude influences from mainstream genres such as rock.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Many insist that bluegrass is defined by its adherence to the folk music of the US South, out of which bluegrass emerged.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Such “purists,” as they are known, regard the recordings of Bill Monroe, which established the bluegrass sound in the 1940s, as a standard against which the genre should still be measured.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Bluegrass isn’t simply an extension of folk traditions into the era of recorded music.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: In reality, Bill Monroe created the bluegrass sound in the 1940s by combining Southern folk music with commercial genres that had arisen only a few decades before, such as jazz and the blues.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Since bluegrass has always been a mixed genre, contemporary bluegrass musicians should not be forbidden from incorporating into it influences from rock and other mainstream genres.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: Most scientists agree that the moon was likely formed after a collision between Earth and a large planet named Theia.

sentence_analysis.text: This collision likely created a huge debris field, made up of material from both Earth and Theia.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Literary scholars have struggled with the vastness of Nigerian writer Wole Soyinka’s collective works of drama (spanning over 20 plays in total).
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: It is best, however, to understand Soyinka’s body of work as a dramatist chronologically.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Soyinka’s progression as a playwright can be considered to fall into three periods, with each one representing a particular thematic and stylistic cohesion: the 1960s, the two decades between 1970 and 1990, and lastly, from roughly 1990 onwards.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: It is tempting to impose a linear sense of order on the expanse of Wole Soyinka’s body of work as a dramatist.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: However, critics who have considered Soyinka’s plays to fit neatly into three phases overlook potential commonalities in Soyinka’s work that span across these phases.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Additionally, this view may discount significant differences in the styles and content of plays written around the same time.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: In a study of insect behavior, Samadi Galpayage and colleagues presented bumblebees with small wooden balls and observed many of the bees clinging to, rolling, and dragging the objects.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The researchers provided no external rewards (such as food) to encourage these interactions.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: The bees simply appeared to be playing—and for no other reason than because they were having fun.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Insects do not have cortexes or other brain areas associated with emotions in humans.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Still, Galpayage and her team have shown that bumblebees may engage in play, possibly experiencing some kind of positive emotional state.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Other studies have suggested that bees experience negative emotional states (for example, stress), but as Galpayage and her team have acknowledged, emotions in insects, if they do indeed exist, are likely very rudimentary.
sentence_analysis.label: Concession

sentence_analysis.text: Although food writing is one of the most widely read genres in the United States, literary scholars have long neglected it.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: And within this genre, cookbooks attract the least scholarly attention of all, regardless of how well written they may be.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: This is especially true of works dedicated to regional US cuisines, whose complexity and historical significance are often overlooked.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: With her 1976 cookbook The Taste of Country Cooking, Edna Lewis popularized the refined Southern cooking she had grown up with in Freetown, an all-Black community in Virginia.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: She also set a new standard for cookbook writing: the recipes and memoir passages interspersing them are written in prose more elegant than that of most novels.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Yet despite its inarguable value as a piece of writing, Lewis’s masterpiece has received almost no attention from literary scholars.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: Some animal species, like the leopard, can be found in many kinds of areas.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: On the other hand, tropical mountain bird species tend to be limited in the types of spaces they can call home.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: This is because many mountain bird species are only able to survive at very specific elevations.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Over time, these species have likely become used to living at a specific temperature.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: Therefore, these species struggle to survive at elevations that are warmer or colder than they are used to.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: A new study reviewed observations of nearly 3,000 bird species to understand why tropical mountain bird species live at specific elevations.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: They noted that when a mountain bird species was found in an area with many other bird species, it tended to inhabit much smaller geographic areas.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: It is thus likely that competition for resources with other species, not temperature, limits where these birds can live.
sentence_analysis.label: Conclusion

sentence_analysis.text: American sculptor Edmonia Lewis is best known for her sculptures that represent figures from history and mythology,
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: such as The Death of Cleopatra and Hagar.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: Although Lewis sculpted other subjects, her career as a sculptor is best represented by the works in which she depicted these historical and mythical themes.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Art historians have typically ignored the many portrait busts Edmonia Lewis created.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: Lewis likely carved these busts (sculptures of a person’s head) frequently throughout her long career.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: She is known for her sculptures that represent historical figures, but Lewis likely supported herself financially by carving portrait busts for acquaintances who paid her to represent their features.
sentence_analysis.label: Concession

sentence_analysis.text: Thus, Lewis’s portrait busts are a central aspect of her career as a sculptor.
sentence_analysis.label: Conclusion

sentence_analysis.text: A team led by Bernardo Strassburg has found that rewilding farmland (returning the land to its natural state) could help preserve biodiversity and offset carbon emissions.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The amount of farmland that would need to be restored, they found, is remarkably low.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Rewilding a mere 15% of the world’s current farmland would prevent 60% of expected species extinctions and help absorb nearly 299 gigatons of carbon dioxide—a clear win in the fight against the biodiversity and climate crises.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: While Strassburg’s team’s findings certainly offer encouraging insight into the potential benefits of rewilding, it’s important to consider potential effects on global food supplies.
sentence_analysis.label: Contrast

sentence_analysis.text: The researchers suggest that to compensate for the loss of food-producing land, remaining farmland would need to produce even more food.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: Thus, policies focused on rewilding farmland must also address strategies for higher-yield farming.
sentence_analysis.label: Conclusion

sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Price continued to compose many musical pieces throughout her career, blending traditional Black spirituals with classical European Romantic musical traditions.

sentence_analysis.text: In recent years, Price’s concertos and symphonies have been performed and recorded by several major orchestras, further preserving her work for others to enjoy.

sentence_analysis.text: Some bird species don’t raise their own chicks.

sentence_analysis.text: Female cuckoos have been seen quickly laying eggs in the nests of other bird species when those birds are out looking for food.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: After the eggs hatch, the noncuckoo parents will typically raise the cuckoo chicks as if they were their own offspring, even if the cuckoos look very different from the other chicks.

sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: But life is calling you!

sentence_analysis.text: People whose desire is solely for self-realisation never know where they are going.

sentence_analysis.text: In most building demolitions, the building materials are destroyed and sent to landfills.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: City officials in Portland, Oregon, wanted to reduce this waste.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The officials passed a law requiring demolition companies to deconstruct some buildings instead.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: Deconstruction involves carefully taking buildings apart piece by piece.
sentence_analysis.label: Definition

sentence_analysis.text: Damage to the materials is avoided so that they can be reused in new constructions.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: A 2019 study found that 27 percent of materials from deconstructions in Portland were able to be reused.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: The remaining materials were processed for recycling instead of going to a landfill.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: More than two years ago my parents bought a piano from some people who were moving to Utah.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Mom and Dad gave it to my brothers and me for Christmas.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: I had to act really happy because it was such a big present, but I pretty much hated the thing from the second it was carried into the hallway upstairs, which is right next to my bedroom.
sentence_analysis.label: Contrast

sentence_analysis.text: The piano glared at me.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: It was like a songbird in a cage.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: It wanted to be set free.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Were penguins always flightless?
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: Theresa Cole and her team argue that penguins could fly at some point, but that they lost that ability more than 60 million years ago as they adapted to marine life.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Streams and rivers carry soil and rocks from one location to another.

sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: Geologist Melisa Diaz and her team studied dust in Antarctica to find out if it was moved by aeolian transport.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: They discovered that the dust matched geological material in Australia.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Aeolian transport had carried it from one continent to another, across thousands of miles of open ocean.
sentence_analysis.label: Conclusion

sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Dr. Rocío Paola Caballero-Gill is a paleoceanographer.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: This means that Dr. Caballero-Gill doesn’t just study oceans as they are today.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: She uses chemistry and fossil evidence ______ oceans as they were in the past.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: The Boston Saloon was one of the most popular African American–owned establishments in nineteenth-century Nevada.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: ______ by businessman William A.G. Brown, the saloon was known to offer elegant accommodations and an inclusive environment.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: In 1916, H. Dugdale Sykes disputed claims that The Two Noble Kinsmen was coauthored by William Shakespeare and John Fletcher.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Sykes felt Fletcher’s contributions to the play were obvious—Fletcher had a distinct style in his other plays, so much so that lines with that style were considered sufficient evidence of Fletcher’s authorship.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: But for the lines not deemed to be by Fletcher, Sykes felt that their depiction of women indicated that their author was not Shakespeare but Philip Massinger.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Scholars have accepted The Two Noble Kinsmen as coauthored by Shakespeare since the 1970s: it appears in all major one-volume editions of Shakespeare’s complete works.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Though scholars disagree about who wrote what exactly, it is generally held that on the basis of style, Shakespeare wrote all of the first act and most of the last, while John Fletcher authored most of the three middle acts.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Growth in the use of novel nanohybrids—materials created from the conjugation of multiple distinct nanomaterials, such as iron oxide and gold nanomaterials conjugated for use in magnetic imaging—has outpaced studies of nanohybrids’ environmental risks.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Unfortunately, risk evaluations based on nanohybrids’ constituents are not reliable: conjugation may alter constituents’ physiochemical properties such that innocuous nanomaterials form a nanohybrid that is anything but.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The potential for enhanced toxicity of nanohybrids relative to the toxicity of constituent nanomaterials has drawn deserved attention, but the effects of nanomaterial conjugation vary by case.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: For instance, it was recently shown that a nanohybrid of silicon dioxide and zinc oxide preserved the desired optical transparency of zinc oxide nanoparticles while mitigating the nanoparticles’ potential to damage DNA.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: Africa’s Sahara region—once a lush ecosystem—began to dry out about 8,000 years ago.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: A change in Earth’s orbit that affected climate has been posited as a cause of desertification, but archaeologist David Wright also attributes the shift to Neolithic peoples.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: He cites their adoption of pastoralism as a factor in the region drying out: the pastoralists’ livestock depleted vegetation, prompting the events that created the Sahara Desert.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Research by Chris Brierley et al. challenges the idea that Neolithic peoples contributed to the Sahara’s desertification.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Using a climate-vegetation model, the team concluded that the end of the region’s humid period occurred 500 years earlier than previously assumed.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: The timing suggests that Neolithic peoples didn’t exacerbate aridity in the region but, in fact, may have helped delay environmental changes with practices (e.g., selective grazing) that preserved vegetation.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: Soy sauce, made from fermented soybeans, is noted for its umami flavor.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Umami—one of the five basic tastes along with sweet, bitter, salty, and sour—was formally classified when its taste receptors were discovered in the 2000s.
sentence_analysis.label: Definition

sentence_analysis.text: In 2007, to define the pure umami flavor scientists Rie Ishii and Michael O’Mahony used broths made from shiitake mushrooms and kombu seaweed, and two panels of Japanese and US judges closely agreed on a description of the taste.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: A 2022 experiment by Manon Jünger et al. led to a greater understanding of soy sauce’s flavor profile.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The team initially presented a mixture of compounds with low molecular weights to taste testers who found it was not as salty or bitter as real soy sauce.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Further analysis of soy sauce identified proteins, including dipeptides, that enhanced umami flavor and also contributed to saltiness.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: The team then made a mix of 50 chemical compounds that re-created soy sauce’s flavor.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: Astronomer Mark Holland and colleagues examined four white dwarfs—small, dense remnants of past stars—in order to determine the composition of exoplanets that used to orbit those stars.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Studying wavelengths of light in the white dwarf atmospheres, the team reported that traces of elements such as lithium and sodium support the presence of exoplanets with continental crusts similar to Earth’s.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Past studies of white dwarf atmospheres have concluded that certain exoplanets had continental crusts.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Geologist Keith Putirka and astronomer Siyi Xu argue that those studies unduly emphasize atmospheric traces of lithium and other individual elements as signifiers of the types of rock found on Earth.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The studies don’t adequately account for different minerals made up of various ratios of those elements, and the possibility of rock types not found on Earth that contain those minerals.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: Mycoprotein is a fungal biomass that can be eaten as an alternative to meat.
sentence_analysis.label: Definition

sentence_analysis.text: Studies of the environmental impact of its manufacture generally agree it is lower than that of beef and closer to that of chicken or pork.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: But the expense of producing mycoprotein restricts its availability to a few countries with postindustrial economies.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: Knowing that cost reductions would expand access to mycoprotein, biochemists are exploring solutions, such as a cheaper substrate to feed the mycoprotein as it grows.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: Cattle farming is a principal cause of global deforestation, and a study by Florian Humpenöder and his colleagues found that replacing 20% of beef consumption worldwide with consumption of mycoprotein would cut deforestation by half if accomplished over the next thirty years.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: However, this would likely involve only a small change in agricultural water consumption, since water once dedicated to raising cattle would be diverted to raising crops instead.
sentence_analysis.label: Contrast

sentence_analysis.text: Fossils of the hominin Australopithecus africanus have been found in the Sterkfontein Caves of South Africa, but assigning an age to the fossils is challenging because of the unreliability of dating methods in this context.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The geology of Sterkfontein has caused soil layers from different periods to mix, impeding stratigraphic dating, and dates cannot be reliably imputed from those of nearby animal bones since the bones may have been relocated by flooding.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: Archaeologists used new cosmogenic nuclide dating techniques to reevaluate the ages of A. africanus fossils found in the Sterkfontein Caves.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: This technique involves analyzing the cosmogenic nucleotides in the breccia—the matrix of rock fragments immediately surrounding the fossils.
sentence_analysis.label: Definition

sentence_analysis.text: The researchers assert that this approach avoids the potential for misdating associated with assigning ages based on Sterkfontein’s soil layers or animal bones.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Films and television shows commonly include a long list of credits naming the people involved in a production.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Credit sequences may not be exciting, but they generally ensure that everyone’s contributions are duly acknowledged.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Because they are highly standardized, film and television credits are also valuable to anyone researching the careers of pioneering cast and crew members who have worked in the mediums.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Video game scholars face a major challenge in the industry’s failure to consistently credit the artists, designers, and other contributors involved in making video games.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: Without a reliable record of which people worked on which games, questions about the medium’s development can be difficult to answer, and the accomplishments of all but its best-known innovators can be difficult to trace.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: The Cretaceous-Paleogene (K-Pg) mass extinction event is usually attributed solely to an asteroid impact near Chicxulub, Mexico.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Some scientists argue that volcanic activity was the true cause, as the K-Pg event occurred relatively early in a long period of eruption of the Deccan Traps range that initially produced huge amounts of climate-altering gases.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: These dissenters note that other mass extinctions have coincided with large volcanic eruptions, while only the K-Pg event lines up with an asteroid strike.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: In a 2020 study, Pincelli Hull and her colleagues analyzed ocean core samples and modeled climate changes around the K-Pg event.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: The team concluded that Deccan Traps gases did affect global conditions prior to the event, but that the climate returned to normal well before the extinctions began—extinctions that instead closely align with the Chicxulub impact.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Like the work of Ralph Ellison before her, Toni Morrison’s novels feature scenes in which characters deliver sermons of such length and verbal dexterity that for a time, the text exchanges the formal parameters of fiction for those of oral literature.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Given the many other echoes of Ellison in Morrison’s novels, both in structure and prose style, these scenes suggest Ellison’s direct influence on Morrison.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: In their destabilizing effect on literary form, the sermons in Morrison’s works recall those in Ellison’s.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Yet literature by Black Americans abounds in moments where interpolated speech erodes the division between oral and written forms that literature in English has traditionally observed.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Morrison’s use of the sermon is attributable not only to the influence of Ellison but also to a community-wide strategy of resistance to externally imposed literary conventions.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Virginia Woolf’s 1928 novel Orlando is an oddity within her body of work.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Her other major novels consist mainly of scenes of everyday life and describe their characters’ interior states in great detail, whereas Orlando propels itself through a series of fantastical events and considers its characters’ psychology more superficially.
sentence_analysis.label: Contrast

sentence_analysis.text: Woolf herself sometimes regarded the novel as a minor work, even admitting once that she 'began it as a joke.'
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Like Woolf’s other great novels, Orlando portrays how people’s memories inform their experience of the present.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Like those works, it examines how people navigate social interactions shaped by gender and social class.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Though it is lighter in tone—more entertaining, even—this literary 'joke' nonetheless engages seriously with the themes that motivated the four or five other novels by Woolf that have achieved the status of literary classics.
sentence_analysis.label: Concession

sentence_analysis.text: Most animals can regenerate some parts of their bodies, such as skin.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: But when a three-banded panther worm is cut into three pieces, each piece grows into a new worm.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Researchers are investigating this feat partly to learn more about humans’ comparatively limited abilities to regenerate, and they’re making exciting progress.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: An especially promising discovery is that both humans and panther worms have a gene for early growth response (EGR) linked to regeneration.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: When Mansi Srivastava and her team reported that panther worms, like humans, possess a gene for EGR, it caused excitement.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: However, as the team pointed out, the gene likely functions very differently in humans than it does in panther worms.
sentence_analysis.label: Contrast

sentence_analysis.text: Srivastava has likened EGR to a switch that activates other genes involved in regeneration in panther worms, but how this switch operates in humans remains unclear.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: Despite its beautiful prose, The Guns of August, Barbara Tuchman’s 1962 analysis of the start of World War I, has certain weaknesses as a work of history.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: It fails to address events in Eastern Europe just before the outbreak of hostilities, thereby giving the impression that Germany was the war’s principal instigator.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: Had Tuchman consulted secondary works available to her by scholars such as Luigi Albertini, she would not have neglected the influence of events in Eastern Europe on Germany’s actions.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: Barbara Tuchman’s The Guns of August is an engrossing if dated introduction to World War I.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Tuchman’s analysis of primary documents is laudable, but her main thesis that European powers committed themselves to a catastrophic outcome by refusing to deviate from military plans developed prior to the conflict is implausibly reductive.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: In 2007, a team led by Alice Storey analyzed a chicken bone found in El Arenal, Chile, dating it to 1321–1407 CE—over a century before Europeans invaded the region, bringing their own chickens.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Storey also found that the El Arenal chicken shared a unique genetic mutation with the ancient chicken breeds of the Polynesian Islands in the Pacific.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Thus, Polynesian peoples, not later Europeans, probably first introduced chickens to South America.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: An Australian research team weakened the case for a Polynesian origin for the El Arenal chicken by confirming that the mutation identified by Storey has occurred in breeds from around the world.
sentence_analysis.label: Contrast

sentence_analysis.text: More recently, though, a team led by Agusto Luzuriaga-Neira found that South American chicken breeds and Polynesian breeds share other genetic markers that European breeds lack.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Thus, the preponderance of evidence now favors a Polynesian origin.
sentence_analysis.label: Conclusion

sentence_analysis.text: Conventional wisdom long held that human social systems evolved in stages, beginning with hunter-gatherers forming small bands of members with roughly equal status.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The shift to agriculture about 12,000 years ago sparked population growth that led to the emergence of groups with hierarchical structures: associations of clans first, then chiefdoms, and finally, bureaucratic states.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: In a 2021 book, anthropologist David Graeber and archaeologist David Wengrow maintain that humans have always been socially flexible, alternately forming systems based on hierarchy and collective ones with decentralized leadership.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The authors point to evidence that as far back as 50,000 years ago some hunter-gatherers adjusted their social structures seasonally, at times dispersing in small groups but also assembling into communities that included esteemed individuals.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: The fossil record suggests that mammoths went extinct around 11 thousand years (kyr) ago.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: In a 2021 study of environmental DNA (eDNA)—genetic material shed into the environment by organisms—in the Arctic, Yucheng Wang and colleagues found mammoth eDNA in sedimentary layers formed millennia later, around 4 kyr ago.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: To account for this discrepancy, Joshua H. Miller and Carl Simpson proposed that arctic temperatures could preserve a mammoth carcass on the surface, allowing it to leach DNA into the environment, for several thousand years.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: Wang and colleagues concede that eDNA contains DNA from both living organisms and carcasses, but for DNA to leach from remains over several millennia requires that the remains be perpetually on the surface.
sentence_analysis.label: Concession

sentence_analysis.text: Scavengers and weathering in the Arctic, however, are likely to break down surface remains well before a thousand years have passed.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: Ecologists have long wondered how thousands of microscopic phytoplankton species can live together near ocean surfaces competing for the same resources.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Dominique Potvin and colleagues captured five Australian magpies (Gymnorhina tibicen) to test a new design for attaching tracking devices to birds.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: As the researchers fitted each magpie with a tracker attached by a small harness, they noticed some magpies without trackers pecking at another magpie’s tracker until it broke off.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: The researchers suggest that this behavior could be evidence of magpies attempting to help another magpie without benefiting themselves.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: It can be tempting to think that animals are deliberately providing help when we see them removing trackers and other equipment from one another, especially when a species is known to exhibit other cooperative behaviors.
sentence_analysis.label: Concession

sentence_analysis.text: At the same time, it can be difficult to exclude the possibility that individuals are simply interested in the equipment because of its novelty, curiously pawing or pecking at it until it detaches.
sentence_analysis.label: Contrast

sentence_analysis.text: “How lifelike are they?” Many computer animators prioritize this question as they strive to create ever more realistic environments and lighting.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Generally, while characters in computer-animated films appear highly exaggerated, environments and lighting are carefully engineered to mimic reality.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: But some animators, such as Pixar’s Sanjay Patel, are focused on a different question.
sentence_analysis.label: Contrast

sentence_analysis.text: Rather than asking first whether the environments and lighting they’re creating are convincingly lifelike, Patel and others are asking whether these elements reflect their films’ unique stories.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The field of study called affective neuroscience seeks instinctive, physiological causes for feelings such as pleasure or displeasure.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Because these sensations are linked to a chemical component (for example, the release of the neurotransmitter dopamine in the brain when one receives or expects a reward), they can be said to have a partly physiological basis.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: These processes have been described in mammals, but Jingnan Huang and his colleagues have recently observed that some behaviors of honeybees (such as foraging) are also motivated by a dopamine-based signaling process.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Studying late nineteenth- and early twentieth-century artifacts from an agricultural and domestic site in Texas,
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: archaeologist Ayana O. Flewellen found that Black women employed as farm workers utilized hook-and-eye closures to fasten their clothes at the waist, giving themselves a silhouette similar to the one that was popular in contemporary fashion and typically achieved through more restrictive garments such as corsets.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Flewellen argues that this sartorial practice shows that these women balanced hegemonic ideals of femininity with the requirements of their physically demanding occupation.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: In 2020, rap artist and professor A.D. Carson published the first peer-reviewed rap album about his experiences with Black masculinity called “i used to love to dream.”
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Typically in peer review, experts evaluate scholarly articles prior to publication.
sentence_analysis.label: Definition

sentence_analysis.text: For Carson’s album, dubbed a “mixtap/e/ssay,” peer review involved both scholars and rap artists.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: In combining elements of a mixtape album with scholarly essays that connect Carson’s lyrics to historical and contemporary contexts for listeners both inside and outside academia, Carson’s album helped redefine how scholarship is created and shared.
sentence_analysis.label: Conclusion

sentence_analysis.text: Astronomers are confident that the star Betelgeuse will eventually consume all the helium in its core and explode in a supernova.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: They are much less confident, however, about when this will happen, since that depends on internal characteristics of Betelgeuse that are largely unknown.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: Astrophysicist Sarafina El-Badry Nance and colleagues recently investigated whether acoustic waves in the star could be used to determine internal stellar states but concluded that this method could not sufficiently reveal Betelgeuse’s internal characteristics to allow its evolutionary state to be firmly fixed.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: The following text is from Charlotte Brontë’s 1847 novel Jane Eyre.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Jane, the narrator, works as a governess at Thornfield Hall.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: I went on with my day’s business tranquilly; but ever and anon vague suggestions kept wandering across my brain of reasons why I should quit Thornfield;
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: and I kept involuntarily framing advertisements and pondering conjectures about new situations:
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: these thoughts I did not think to check;
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: they might germinate and bear fruit if they could.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: The following text is adapted from Herman Melville’s 1857 novel The Confidence-Man.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Humphry Davy was a prominent British chemist and inventor.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Years ago, a grave American savant, being in London, observed at an evening party there, a certain coxcombical fellow, as he thought, an absurd ribbon in his lapel, and full of smart [banter], whisking about to the admiration of as many as were disposed to admire.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Great was the savant’s disdain; but, chancing ere long to find himself in a corner with the jackanapes, got into conversation with him, when he was somewhat ill-prepared for the good sense of the jackanapes, but was altogether thrown aback, upon subsequently being [informed that he was] no less a personage than Sir Humphry Davy.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: The following text is adapted from Herman Melville’s 1855 novel Israel Potter.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Israel is a young man wandering through New England during the late eighteenth century.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: He hired himself out for three months; at the end of that time to receive for his wages two hundred acres of land lying in New Hampshire.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: His employer proving false to the contract in the matter of the land, and there being no law in the country to force him to fulfil it,
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: Israel—who, however brave-hearted, and even much of a dare-devil upon a pinch, seems nevertheless to have evinced, throughout many parts of his career, a singular patience and mildness—
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: was obliged to look round for other means of livelihood than clearing out a farm for himself in the wilderness.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: Some studies have suggested that posture can influence cognition, but we should not overstate this phenomenon.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: A case in point: In a 2014 study, Megan O’Brien and Alaa Ahmed had subjects stand or sit while making risky simulated economic decisions.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: Standing is more physically unstable and cognitively demanding than sitting; accordingly, O’Brien and Ahmed hypothesized that standing subjects would display more risk aversion during the decision-making tasks than sitting subjects did, since they would want to avoid further feelings of discomfort and complicated risk evaluations.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: But O’Brien and Ahmed actually found no difference in the groups’ performance.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: In Jane Austen’s novel Mansfield Park, an almost imperceptible smile from potential suitor Henry Crawford causes the protagonist Fanny Price to blush; her embarrassment grows when she suspects that he is aware of it.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: This moment—in which Fanny not only infers Henry’s mental state through his gestures, but also infers that he is drawing inferences about her mental state—illustrates what literary scholar George Butte calls 'deep intersubjectivity,'
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: a technique for representing interactions between consciousnesses through which Austen’s novels derive much of their social and psychological drama.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: The following text is from Edith Wharton’s 1905 novel The House of Mirth.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Lily had no real intimacy with nature, but she had a passion for the appropriate and could be keenly sensitive to a scene which was the fitting background of her own sensations.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The landscape outspread below her seemed an enlargement of her present mood, and she found something of herself in its calmness, its breadth, its long free reaches.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: On the nearer slopes the sugar-maples wavered like pyres of light; lower down was a massing of grey orchards, and here and there the lingering green of an oak-grove.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: Changes to vegetation cover and other human activities influence carbon and nitrogen levels in soil, though how deep these effects extend is unclear.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Hypothesizing that differences in land use lead to differences in carbon and nitrogen levels that are not restricted to the topsoil layer (0–30 cm deep), Chukwuebuka Okolo and colleagues sampled soils across multiple land-use types (e.g., grazing land, cropland, forest) within each of several Ethiopian locations.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: They found, though, that across land-use types, carbon and nitrogen decreased to comparably low levels beyond depths of 30 cm.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Historians have argued that a crucial component of the Civil Rights Movement’s success in the 1960s was the Southern Christian Leadership Conference’s Citizen Education Program (CEP), which invited promising activists from across the South to its one-week training sessions in Dorchester, Georgia.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Led by experienced organizers such as Dorothy Cotton and Septima Clark, CEP attendees—more than 7,000 in all—participated in workshops on topics ranging from public speaking to legal doctrine before returning home and using their newly acquired knowledge to spearhead local civil rights initiatives.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Mathematician Claude Shannon is widely regarded as a foundational figure in information theory.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: His most important paper, “A Mathematical Theory of Communication,” published in 1948 when he was employed at Bell Labs, utilized a concept called a “binary digit” (shortened to “bit”) to measure the amount of information in any signal and determine the fastest rate at which information could be transmitted while still being reliably decipherable.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Robert Gallagher, one of Shannon’s colleagues, said that the bit was “[Shannon’s] discovery, and from it the whole communications revolution has sprung.”
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: A study by a team including finance professor Madhu Veeraraghavan suggests that exposure to sunshine during the workday can lead to overly optimistic behavior.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Using data spanning from 1994 to 2010 for a set of US companies, the team compared over 29,000 annual earnings forecasts to the actual earnings later reported by those companies.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: The team found that the greater the exposure to sunshine at work in the two weeks before a manager submitted an earnings forecast, the more the manager’s forecast exceeded what the company actually earned that year.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: The following text is adapted from Zora Neale Hurston’s 1921 short story “John Redding Goes to Sea.”
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: John is a child who lives in a town in the woods.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Perhaps ten-year-old John was puzzling to the folk there in the Florida woods for he was an imaginative child and fond of day-dreams.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The St. John River flowed a scarce three hundred feet from his back door.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: On its banks at this point grow numerous palms, luxuriant magnolias and bay trees.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: On the bosom of the stream float millions of delicately colored hyacinths.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: [John Redding] loved to wander down to the water’s edge, and, casting in dry twigs, watch them sail away down stream to Jacksonville, the sea, the wide world and [he] wanted to follow them.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: A number of Indigenous politicians have been elected to the United States Congress since 2000 as members of the country’s two established political parties.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: In Canada and several Latin American countries, on the other hand, Indigenous people have formed their own political parties to advance candidates who will advocate for the interests of their communities.
sentence_analysis.label: Contrast

sentence_analysis.text: This movement has been particularly successful in Ecuador, where Guadalupe Llori, a member of the Indigenous party known as Pachakutik, was elected president of the National Assembly in 2021.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: The following text is adapted from Indian Boyhood, a 1902 memoir by Ohiyesa (Charles A. Eastman), a Santee Dakota writer.

sentence_analysis.text: The mineral mtorolite is most commonly found in Zimbabwe.

sentence_analysis.text: contaminated soil can be detoxified via phytoremediation: plants that can withstand high concentrations of metals absorb the pollutants and store them in their shoots, which are then cut off and safely disposed of, preserving the health of the plants.

sentence_analysis.text: Magnetic levitation (maglev) trains are suspended above a track by powerful electromagnets, reducing friction and thus allowing for much faster speeds.

sentence_analysis.text: Though maglev advocates in the US have long imagined these trains crisscrossing the country, their dream remains unrealized.

sentence_analysis.text: her poem “Elegy for a Woman of No Importance” consists of two ten-line stanzas and a standard number of syllables.

sentence_analysis.text: Even in this superficially traditional work, Al-Malaika was breaking new ground by memorializing an anonymous woman rather than a famous man.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: A 2017 study of sign language learners tested the role of iconicity—the similarity of a sign to the thing it represents—in language acquisition.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The study found that the greater the iconicity of a sign, the more likely it was to have been learned.

sentence_analysis.text: ______ the correlation between acquisition and iconicity was lower than that between acquisition and another factor studied: sign frequency.

sentence_analysis.text: Historically, most conductors of major orchestras and opera companies have been European men, but a new, more diverse generation of artists is stepping up to the podium.

sentence_analysis.text: Mexico’s Alondra de la Parra took over as conductor for the Queensland Symphony Orchestra in 2017, and Colombia’s Lina Gonzalez-Granados did the same for the Los Angeles Opera in 2022.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: “Tulip mania”—the rapid rise and sudden fall of the price of tulip bulbs in seventeenth-century Amsterdam—is often cited
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: as an example of the perils of rampant market speculation.

sentence_analysis.text: To perform a quad axel, a figure skater must leap into the air and complete four and a half rotations before landing, an extreme feat.
sentence_analysis.label: Definition

sentence_analysis.text: In 2022, when 17-year-old Ilia Malinin landed the first quad axel—considered the most difficult quad jump—in a high-level competition, the audience was left awestruck.

sentence_analysis.text: Seismologists Kaiqing Yuan and Barbara Romanowicz have proposed that the magma fueling Iceland’s more than 30 active volcano systems emerges from deep within Earth.

sentence_analysis.text: The great depths involved—nearly 3,000 km—mark Iceland’s volcanoes as extreme outliers;

sentence_analysis.text: With its clichéd imagery of suburban lawns and power lines, John Ashbery’s 2004 poem “Ignorance of the Law Is No Excuse” may seem barren terrain for critical analysis.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Cultural critic Lauren Berlant finds fertile ground in just its first two stanzas, devoting most of a book chapter to deciphering the “weight of the default space” Ashbery creates in this poem.

sentence_analysis.text: In response to adverse environmental conditions, many plants produce abscisic acid (ABA), a stress hormone.

sentence_analysis.text: ABA triggers a slowdown in the biological processes of most plants.

sentence_analysis.text: The Sun and other stars are powered by nuclear fusion reactions, in which two atoms collide to form a single heavier atom, releasing energy.

sentence_analysis.text: Scientists have long believed that fusion has the potential to meet humanity’s clean energy needs.

sentence_analysis.text: rather than just focusing on the human genome, efforts to better understand gene mutations related to disease have begun to consider the human proteome, the complete set of proteins expressed by human genes.

sentence_analysis.text: Plato believed material objects to be crude representations of unseen ideal forms.

sentence_analysis.text: In his view, such abstract, nonmaterial forms are the ultimate source of knowledge.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Aristotle disagreed, positing that knowledge is best obtained through direct engagement with the material world;

sentence_analysis.text: The most recent iteration of the immersive theater experience Sleep No More, which premiered in New York City in 2011, transforms its performance space—a five-story warehouse—into a 1930s-era hotel.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Audience members, who wander through the labyrinthine venue at their own pace and follow the actors as they play out simultaneous, interweaving narrative loops, confront the impossibility of experiencing the production in its entirety.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: To understand how temperature change affects microorganism-mediated cycling of soil nutrients in alpine ecosystems,
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Eva Kaštovská et al. collected plant-soil cores in the Tatra Mountains at elevations around 2,100 meters and transplanted them to elevations of 1,700–1,800 meters, where the mean air temperature was warmer by 2°C.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Microorganism-mediated nutrient cycling was accelerated in the transplanted cores; crucially, microorganism community composition was unchanged, allowing Kaštovská et al. to attribute the acceleration to temperature-induced increases in microorganism activity.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Many literary theorists distinguish between fabula, a narrative’s content, and syuzhet, a narrative’s arrangement and presentation of events.
sentence_analysis.label: Definition

sentence_analysis.text: In the film The Godfather Part II, the fabula is the story of the Corleone family, and the syuzhet is the presentation of the story as it alternates between two timelines in 1901 and 1958.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: But literary theorist Mikhail Bakhtin maintained that fabula and syuzhet are insufficient to completely describe a narrative—he held that systematic categorizations of artistic phenomena discount the subtle way in which meaning is created by interactions between the artist, the work, and the audience.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The following text is adapted from María Cristina Mena’s 1914 short story “The Vine-Leaf.”
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: It is a saying in the capital of Mexico that Dr. Malsufrido carries more family secrets under his hat than any archbishop.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The doctor’s hat is, appropriately enough, uncommonly capacious, rising very high, and sinking so low that it seems to be supported by his ears and eyebrows, and it has a furry look, as if it had been brushed the wrong way, which is perhaps what happens to it if it is ever brushed at all.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: When the doctor takes it off, the family secrets do not fly out like a flock of parrots, but remain nicely bottled up beneath a dome of old and highly polished ivory.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: The following text is adapted from Countee Cullen’s 1926 poem “Thoughts in a Zoo.”
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: They in their cruel traps, and we in ours, Survey each other’s rage, and pass the hours Commiserating each the other’s woe, To mitigate his own pain’s fiery glow.

sentence_analysis.text: Man could but little proffer in exchange Save that his cages have a larger range.
sentence_analysis.label: Contrast

sentence_analysis.text: That lion with his lordly, untamed heart Has in some man his human counterpart,
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Some lofty soul in dreams and visions wrapped, But in the stifling flesh securely trapped.

sentence_analysis.text: In superfluorescence, electrical charges known as dipoles emit light in synchronized bursts so intense that they are visible to the eye.
sentence_analysis.label: Definition

sentence_analysis.text: Until recently, this phenomenon has only been observed at extremely cold temperatures because dipoles cannot synchronize at higher temperatures.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: But in a study, Melike Biliroglu and colleagues observed superfluorescence at room temperature in thin films made of perovskite and other similarly crystalline materials;
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: the researchers propose that the formation of shock-absorbing quasiparticles called polarons in the material protects dipoles from thermal interference.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Paleontologist Lucas E. Fiorelli and colleagues have reported the discovery at a mine in Brazil of several egg clutches, partially preserved single eggs, and egg shells from the Late Cretaceous period.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The researchers have concluded that the area was once a nesting and breeding site for titanosaurs, a group of sauropod dinosaurs.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The finding is significant given the previous lack of known nesting sites in northern regions of South America, which led many paleontologists to assume that titanosaurs migrated south to lay eggs.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Elizabeth Asiedu has identified a negative correlation between the share of developing countries’ economies derived from natural-resource extraction and those countries’ receipts of foreign investment.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: This may appear counterintuitive—resource extraction requires initial investments (in extractive technology, for instance) at scales best met by multinational corporations—but Asiedu notes that natural-resource industries’ boom-bust cycle can destabilize local currencies and increase developing countries’ vulnerability to external shocks, creating levels of uncertainty to which foreign investors are typically averse.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: Several scholars have argued that conditions in England in the late ninth through early eleventh centuries—namely, burgeoning literacy amid running conflicts between England’s Anglo-Saxon kingdoms and Danish invaders—were especially conducive to the production of the Old English epic poem Beowulf, and they have dated the poem’s composition accordingly.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: It is not inconceivable that Beowulf emerged from such a context, but privileging contextual fit over the linguistic evidence of an eighth- or even seventh-century composition requires a level of justification that thus far has not been presented.
sentence_analysis.label: Concession

sentence_analysis.text: For centuries, the widespread acknowledgment of the involvement of the cerebellum—a dense brain structure in vertebrates—in coordinating motor control in humans has hindered recognition of other possible functions of the structure.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Neuroscience research from the last two decades now suggests that the cerebellum regulates emotion and social behavior, and recent research by Ilaria Carta and colleagues has identified a pathway connecting the cerebellum to a center for motivation and reward processing known as the ventral tegmental area (VTA).
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Modern dog breeds are largely the result of 160 years of owners crossbreeding certain dogs in order to select for particular physical appearances.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Owners often say that some breeds are also more likely than others to have particular personality traits—basset hounds are affectionate; boxers are easy to train—but Kathleen Morrill and colleagues found through a combination of owner surveys and DNA sequencing of 2,000 dogs that while physical traits are predictably heritable among purebred dogs, behavior varies widely among dogs of the same breed.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: For many years, the only existing fossil evidence of mixopterid eurypterids—an extinct family of large aquatic arthropods known as sea scorpions and related to modern arachnids and horseshoe crabs—came from four species living on the paleocontinent of Laurussia.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: In a discovery that expands our understanding of the geographical distribution of mixopterids, paleontologist Bo Wang and others have identified fossilized remains of a new mixopterid species, Terropterus xiushanensis, that lived over 400 million years ago on the paleocontinent of Gondwana.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Algae living within the tissues of corals play a critical role in keeping corals, and the marine ecosystems they are part of, thriving.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Some coral species appear brown in color when healthy due to the algae colonies living in their tissues.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: In the event of an environmental stressor, the algae can die or be expelled, causing the corals to appear white.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: To recover the algae, the bleached corals then begin to produce bright colors, which block intense sunlight, encouraging the light-sensitive algae to recolonize the corals.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: Having written the impassioned call to arms “Letter to the Spanish Americans” in 1791, Peruvian intellectual Juan Pablo Viscardo y Guzmán is often considered a forerunner for the independence movements in Latin America.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: But Viscardo’s role in history would have remained insignificant were it not for Venezuelan revolutionary Francisco de Miranda, who was handed the unpublished letter after Viscardo’s death.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Miranda not only helped circulate the letter, but his edits and footnotes to the text position Miranda as a central figure in the text’s creation.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Karenin is a dog that belongs to Tomas and Tereza.

sentence_analysis.text: Karenin was not overjoyed by the move to Switzerland [from Prague].

sentence_analysis.text: Karenin hated change.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Dog time cannot be plotted along a straight line; it does not move on and on, from one thing to the next.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: It moves in a circle like the hands of a clock, which—they, too, unwilling to dash madly ahead—turn round and round the face, day in and day out following the same path.

sentence_analysis.text: Disco remains one of the most ridiculed popular music genres of the late twentieth century.

sentence_analysis.text: Take the case of disco icon Donna Summer: she may have been associated with popular songs about love and heartbreak (subjects hardly unique to disco, by the way), but like many Black women singers before her, much of her music also reflects concerns about community and identity.

sentence_analysis.text: These concerns are present in many of the genre’s greatest songs, and they generally don’t require much digging to reveal.

sentence_analysis.text: In a paper about p-i-n planar perovskite solar cells (one of several perovskite cell architectures designed to collect and store solar power), Lyndsey McMillon-Brown et al. describe a method for fabricating the cell’s electronic transport layer (ETL) using a spray coating.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Conventional ETL fabrication is accomplished using a solution of nanoparticles.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The process can result in a loss of up to 80% of the solution, increasing the cost of manufacturing at scale—an issue that may be obviated by spray coating fabrication, which the researchers describe as 'highly reproducible, concise, and practical.'

sentence_analysis.text: Some astronomers searching for extraterrestrial life have proposed that atmospheric NH (ammonia) can serve as a biosignature gas—an indication that a planet harbors life.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Jingcheng Huang, Sara Seager, and colleagues evaluated this possibility, finding that on rocky planets, atmospheric NH likely couldn’t reach detectably high levels in the absence of biological activity.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: But the team also found that on so-called mini-Neptunes—gas planets smaller than Neptune but with atmospheres similar to Neptune’s—atmospheric pressure and temperature can be high enough to produce atmospheric NH.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: In 2019, 20 previously unknown moons were confirmed to be orbiting Saturn.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Three of the moons have prograde orbits (orbiting in the direction the planet spins), and the other 17 have retrograde orbits (orbiting in the opposite direction of the planet’s spin).
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: All but one of the 20 moons are thought to be remnants of bodies that orbited Saturn until they broke apart in collisions.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Although the one exceptional moon orbits in the same direction as the planet’s spin, its orbit is highly eccentric compared to the rest, which may suggest that it has a different origin than the other 19 moons.
sentence_analysis.label: Contrast

sentence_analysis.text: Electronic music pioneer Wendy Carlos is credited with the music for three feature films: A Clockwork Orange (1971), The Shining (1980), and Tron (1982).
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: However, her musical score for A Clockwork Orange is mostly made up of her arrangements of Ludwig van Beethoven’s work.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Also, almost all the music that she and Rachel Elkind composed for The Shining was unused by director Stanley Kubrick.

sentence_analysis.text: It did not appear in the film.

sentence_analysis.text: In a study of new technology adoption, Davit Marikyan et al. examined negative disconfirmation (which occurs when experiences fall short of one’s expectations) to determine whether it could lead to positive outcomes for users.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The team focused on established users of 'smart home' technology, which presents inherent utilization challenges but tends to attract users with high expectations, often leading to feelings of dissonance.

sentence_analysis.text: The researchers found that many users employed cognitive mechanisms to mitigate those feelings, ultimately reversing their initial sense of disappointment.

sentence_analysis.text: Optical tweezers are specialized scientific tools—particularly useful in biology and medicine—that use high-powered beams of light to trap and manipulate minuscule particles for study.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Use of the tool has led to several scientific and medical breakthroughs over the last few decades, but the particles are often under prolonged exposure to the intense heat of the light beams.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: To overcome the risk of overheating, and thereby damage, researchers sometimes attach nano-sized glass beads to particles, allowing the light to focus on the beads instead of the particles.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: Artificial leaves are a developing renewable energy technology that mimics the process of photosynthesis in plants.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: These devices are silicon-based solar cells coated in chemical catalysts that activate reactions that split water molecules into hydrogen and oxygen gas.
sentence_analysis.label: Definition

sentence_analysis.text: The technology, while generating lots of interest, is not yet commercially viable as a large-scale energy source.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: To meet this challenge, scientists from many fields are researching ways to store, transport, and distribute the energy the devices produce while other scientists are working to improve the cost and efficiency of the devices.

sentence_analysis.text: The following text is adapted from Lewis Carroll’s 1889 satirical novel Sylvie and Bruno.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: A crowd has gathered outside a room belonging to the Warden, an official who reports to the Lord Chancellor.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: One man, who was more excited than the rest, flung his hat high into the air, and shouted (as well as I could make out) 'Who roar for the Sub-Warden?'
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Everybody roared, but whether it was for the Sub-Warden, or not, did not clearly appear: some were shouting 'Bread!' and some 'Taxes!', but no one seemed to know what it was they really wanted.
