sentence_analysis.text: All this I saw from the open window of the Warden’s breakfast-saloon, looking across the shoulder of the Lord Chancellor.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: 'What can it all mean?' he kept repeating to himself.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: 'I never heard such shouting before—and at this time of the morning, too! And with such unanimity!'
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: Some animal-behavior studies involve observing wild animals in their natural habitat, and some involve capturing wild animals and observing them in a laboratory.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Each approach has advantages over the other.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: In wild studies, researchers can more easily presume that the animals are behaving normally, and in lab studies, researchers can more easily control factors that might affect the results.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: But if, for example, the results from a wild study and a lab study of Western scrub-jays (Aphelocoma californica) contradict each other, one or both of the studies must have failed to account for some factor that was relevant to the birds’ behavior.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: In the United States, firms often seek incentives from municipal governments to expand to those municipalities.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: A team of political scientists hypothesized that municipalities are much more likely to respond to firms and offer incentives if expansions can be announced in time to benefit local elected officials than if they can’t.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The team contacted officials in thousands of municipalities, inquiring about incentives for a firm looking to expand and indicating that the firm would announce its expansion on a date either just before or just after the next election.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: High levels of public uncertainty about which economic policies a country will adopt can make planning difficult for businesses, but measures of such uncertainty have not tended to be very detailed.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: Recently, however, economist Sandile Hlatshwayo analyzed trends in news reports to derive measures not only for general economic policy uncertainty but also for uncertainty related to specific areas of economic policy, like tax or trade policy.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: One revelation of her work is that a general measure may not fully reflect uncertainty about specific areas of policy, as in the case of the United Kingdom, where general economic policy uncertainty ______
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Number of Lizard Species by Average Percent of Maximal Speed Used When Pursuing Prey or Escaping Predators
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: It may seem that the optimal strategy for an animal pursuing prey or escaping predators is to move at maximal speed,
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: but the energy expense of exploiting full speed capacity can disfavor such a strategy even in escape contexts,
sentence_analysis.label: Contrast

sentence_analysis.text: as evidenced by the fact that ______
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: By comparing the relative concentrations of types of molecules known as nucleobases in the Murchison meteorite with those in the soil, the team concluded that there is evidence that the nucleobases in the Murchison meteorite formed in space and are not the result of contamination on Earth.
sentence_analysis.label: Conclusion

sentence_analysis.text: In 2006, Nitya Kallivayalil and colleagues calculated the most accurate estimate yet of the average velocity (in kilometers per second) of the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) galaxy.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Before the 2006 study, estimates of the average velocity were low enough for the LMC to maintain an orbit around the Milky Way galaxy, but according to an analysis by Gurtina Besla and colleagues, the estimated velocity from the 2006 study is too high for the LMC to maintain such an orbit.

sentence_analysis.text: Therefore, if Besla and colleagues are correct, the maximum average velocity for the LMC that would allow it to maintain orbit around the Milky Way is likely ______.

sentence_analysis.text: Mosasaurs were large marine reptiles that lived in the Late Cretaceous period, approximately 100 million to 66 million years ago.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Celina Suarez, Alberto Pérez-Huerta, and T. Lynn Harrell Jr. examined oxygen-18 isotopes in mosasaur tooth enamel in order to calculate likely mosasaur body temperatures and determined that mosasaurs were endothermic—that is, they used internal metabolic processes to maintain a stable body temperature in a variety of ambient temperatures.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Suarez, Pérez-Huerta, and Harrell claim that endothermy would have enabled mosasaurs to include relatively cold polar waters in their range.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Linguist Deborah Tannen has cautioned against framing contentious issues in terms of two highly competitive perspectives, such as pro versus con.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: In 1534 CE, King Henry VIII of England split with the Catholic Church and declared himself head of the Church of England,
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: in part because Pope Clement VII refused to annul his marriage to Catherine of Aragon.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Two years later, Henry VIII introduced a policy titled the Dissolution of the Monasteries that by 1540 had resulted in the closure of all Catholic monasteries in England and the confiscation of their estates.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Some historians assert that the enactment of the policy was primarily motivated by perceived financial opportunities.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Studying tools unearthed at a cave site on the western coast of Italy, archaeologist Paola Villa and colleagues have determined that prehistoric Neanderthal groups fashioned them from shells of clams that they harvested from the seafloor while wading or diving or that washed up on the beach.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Clamshells become thin and eroded as they wash up on the beach, while those on the seafloor are smooth and sturdy, so the research team suspects that Neanderthals prized the tools made with seafloor shells.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: However, the team also concluded that those tools were likely more challenging to obtain, noting that ______
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: Urbanization, industrialization, and the warming climate create thermal pollution (excess heat) in the shallow subsurface soil.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Susanne A. Benz and colleagues analyzed thousands of sites on three continents under one scenario in which surface temperature remains at the current level and under another in which the surface reaches the maximum plausible temperature.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: They then categorized each site according to the percentage of local home heating needs that could be met using this excess subsurface heat.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The team concluded that if surface temperature approaches the maximum plausible level, the percentage of sites where thermal pollution could feasibly contribute to meeting home heating needs will increase.
sentence_analysis.label: Conclusion

sentence_analysis.text: Research suggests that REM sleep in animals is homeostatically regulated: animals compensate for periods of REM sleep deprivation by increasing subsequent REM sleep.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: When on land, fur seals get enough REM sleep, but during the weeks they’re in the water, they get almost none.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: In a study of fur seals’ sleep habits, researchers recorded the REM sleep (as a percentage of baseline) of fur seals once they had returned to land.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: They concluded that REM sleep may not be homeostatically regulated in fur seals, citing as evidence the fact that the seals in the study ______
sentence_analysis.label: Conclusion

sentence_analysis.text: Neural networks are computer models intended to reflect the organization of human brains and are often used in studies of brain function.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: As media consumption has become increasingly multiplatform and socially mediated, active news acquisition has diminished in favor of an attitude known as 'news finds me' (NFM), in which people passively rely on their social networks and ambient media environments for information about current events.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Homero Gil de Zúñiga and Trevor Diehl examined data on a representative group of adults in the United States to determine participants’ strength of NFM attitude, political knowledge, and political interest.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Although no major election took place sufficiently near the study for Gil de Zúñiga and Diehl to identify causality between NFM and voting behavior, they did posit that NFM may reduce voting probability through an indirect effect.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Over the past two hundred years, the percentage of the population employed in the agricultural sector has declined in both France and the United States, while employment in the service sector (which includes jobs in retail, consulting, real estate, etc.) has risen.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: However, this transition happened at very different rates in the two countries.
sentence_analysis.label: Contrast

sentence_analysis.text: This can be seen most clearly by comparing the employment by sector in both countries in ______
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: In the 1980s, many musicians and journalists in the English-speaking world began to draw attention to music from around the globe—such as mbaqanga from South Africa and quan họ from Vietnam—that can’t be easily categorized according to British or North American popular music genres, typically referring to such music as 'world music.'
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: While some scholars have welcomed this development for bringing diverse musical forms to prominence in countries where they’d previously been overlooked, musicologist Su Zheng claims that the concept of world music homogenizes highly distinct traditions by reducing them all to a single category.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Archaeologist Petra Vaiglova, anthropologist Xinyi Liu, and their colleagues investigated the domestication of farm animals in China during the Bronze Age (approximately 2000 to 1000 BCE).
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: By analyzing the chemical composition of the bones of sheep, goats, and cattle from this era, the team determined that wild plants made up the bulk of sheep’s and goats’ diets, while the cattle’s diet consisted largely of millet, a crop cultivated by humans.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: The team concluded that cattle were likely raised closer to human settlements, whereas sheep and goats were allowed to roam farther away.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Archaeologists have held that the Casarabe culture, which emerged in the southwestern Amazon basin in the first millennium CE, was characterized by a sparse, widely distributed population and little intervention in the surrounding wilderness.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Recently, however, archaeologist Heiko Prümers and colleagues conducted a study of the region using remote-sensing technology that enabled them to create three-dimensional images of the jungle-covered landscape from above, and the researchers concluded that the Casarabe people developed a form of urbanism in the Amazon basin.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: In a research paper, a student criticizes some historians of modern African politics, claiming that they have evaluated Patrice Lumumba, the first prime minister of what is now the Democratic Republic of the Congo, primarily as a symbol rather than in terms of his actions.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Psychologists Dacher Keltner and Jonathan Haidt have argued that experiencing awe—a sensation of reverence and wonder typically brought on by perceiving something grand or powerful—can enable us to feel more connected to others and thereby inspire us to act more altruistically.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Keltner, along with Paul K. Piff, Pia Dietze, and colleagues, claims to have found evidence for this effect in a recent study where participants were asked to either gaze up at exceptionally tall trees in a nearby grove (reported to be a universally awe-inspiring experience) or stare at the exterior of a nearby, nondescript building.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: After one minute, an experimenter deliberately spilled a box of pens nearby.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: Many governments that regularly transfer money to individuals—to provide supplemental incomes for senior citizens, for example—have long done so electronically, but other countries typically have distributed physical money and have only recently developed electronic transfer infrastructure.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Researchers studied the introduction of an electronic transfer system in one such location and found that recipients of electronic transfers consumed a different array of foods than recipients of physical transfers of the same amount did.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: One potential explanation for this result is that individuals conceive of and allocate funds in physical money differently than they conceive of and allocate funds in electronic form.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Icebergs generally appear to be mostly white or blue, depending on how the ice reflects sunlight.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Ice with air bubbles trapped in it looks white because much of the light reflects off the bubbles.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Ice without air bubbles usually looks blue because the light travels deep into the ice and only a little of it is reflected.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: However, some icebergs in the sea around Antarctica appear to be green.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: One team of scientists hypothesized that this phenomenon is the result of yellow-tinted dissolved organic carbon in Antarctic waters mixing with blue ice to produce the color green.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Boldly mixing elements of poetry, fiction, drama, philosophy, and manifesto, Puerto Rican writer Giannina Braschi creates cross-genre literature that explores themes such as immigration and independence.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Her works have inspired responses from individuals across different fields and in a wide range of formats, from musical compositions and a comic book to architecture and furniture design.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: In an essay, a student asserts that the production of these diverse creations by others is reflective of Braschi’s own approach to crafting literature.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Barchester Towers is an 1857 novel by Anthony Trollope.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: In the novel, Trollope’s portrayal of Dr. Proudie underscores the character’s exaggerated sense of his own abilities:
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: An archaeological team led by Piotr Bieliński and Sultan al-Bakri found remnants of a 4,000-year-old Bronze Age board game at a site in Oman.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Little is left of the game except a stone board, which is carved with a grid and has places to hold game pieces.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Some scholars claim that the game was largely played by traders.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: A sociology student is reading an essay on the median age of first marriage in Western countries throughout the twentieth century.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The author of the essay cites factors common to these countries that the author believes caused an increase in the median age of first marriage, such as new technologies that shortened the time needed for domestic chores, making two-person households less necessary and living alone more viable.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The student asserts that beyond these factors there must be additional ones specific to particular Western countries that influenced the increase of age at first marriage.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: In the “language nest” model of education, Indigenous children learn the language of their people by using it as the medium of instruction and socialization at pre-K or elementary levels.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: In their 2016 study of a school in an Anishinaabe community in Ontario, Canada, scholars Lindsay Morcom and Stephanie Roy (who are Anishinaabe themselves) found that the model not only imparted fluency in the Anishinaabe language but also enhanced students’ pride in Anishinaabe culture overall.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Given these positive effects, Morcom and Roy predict that the model increases the probability that as adults, former students of the school will transmit the language to younger generations in their community.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: When digging for clams, their primary food, sea otters damage the roots of eelgrass plants growing on the seafloor.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Near Vancouver Island in Canada, the otter population is large and well established, yet the eelgrass meadows are healthier than those found elsewhere off Canada’s coast.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: To explain this, conservation scientist Erin Foster and colleagues compared the Vancouver Island meadows to meadows where otters are absent or were reintroduced only recently.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Finding that the Vancouver Island meadows have a more diverse gene pool than the others do, Foster hypothesized that damage to eelgrass roots increases the plant’s rate of sexual reproduction; this, in turn, boosts genetic diversity, which benefits the meadow’s health overall.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Mycorrhizal fungi in soil benefits many plants, substantially increasing the mass of some.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: A student conducted an experiment to illustrate this effect.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The student chose three plant species for the experiment, including two that are mycorrhizal hosts (species known to benefit from mycorrhizal fungi) and one nonmycorrhizal species (a species that doesn’t benefit from and may even be harmed by mycorrhizal fungi).
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: The student then grew several plants from each species both in soil containing mycorrhizal fungi and in soil that had been treated to kill mycorrhizal and other fungi.
sentence_analysis.label: Method

sentence_analysis.text: After several weeks, the student measured the plants’ average mass and was surprised to discover that ______
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: The population of the coral Lophelia pertusa declined significantly around 9,000 years ago in the Alboran Sea and around 11,000 years ago near the Mauritanian coast.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Using the ratio of manganese to calcium, which inversely correlates with ocean oxygenation levels, marine scientist Rodrigo da Costa Portilho-Ramos and colleagues evaluated whether oxygenation played a role in the declines of L. pertusa.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The researchers concluded that oxygenation may have been important in the Alboran Sea but not near the Mauritanian coast, since ______
sentence_analysis.label: Conclusion

sentence_analysis.text: Several studies of sediment (e.g., dirt, pieces of rock, etc.) in streams have shown an inverse correlation between sediment grain size and downstream distance from the primary sediment source, suggesting that stream length has a sorting effect on sediment.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: In a study of sediment sampled at more than a dozen sites in Alpine streams, however, geologists Camille Litty and Fritz Schlunegger found that cross-site variations in grain size were not associated with differences in downstream distance, though they did not conclude that downstream distance is irrelevant to grain size.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Rather, they concluded that sediment influx in these streams may have been sufficiently spatially diffuse to prevent the typical sorting effect from being observed.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Political scientists who favor the traditional view of voter behavior claim that voting in an election does not change a voter’s attitude toward the candidates in that election.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Focusing on each US presidential election from 1976 to 1996, Ebonya Washington and Sendhil Mullainathan tested this claim by distinguishing between subjects who had just become old enough to vote (around half of whom actually voted) and otherwise similar subjects who were slightly too young to vote (and thus none of whom voted).
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Washington and Mullainathan compared the attitudes of the groups of subjects toward the winning candidate two years after each election.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Under normal atmospheric pressure at Earth’s surface, water molecules form a tetrahedral network stabilized by hydrogen bonds between adjacent molecules.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Extreme high pressure, such as can be found in deep ocean waters, destabilizes these bonds and compresses water’s structure, allowing water molecules within organisms to permeate proteins and impede crucial biological functions; yet deep-sea organisms known as piezophiles have adapted to extreme pressure.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Studies have found a positive correlation between the depths that various piezophiles inhabit and concentrations of a compound called trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) in their muscle tissues, which has led a team of researchers to hypothesize that TMAO reduces water’s compressibility.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Researchers hypothesized that a decline in the population of dusky sharks near the mid-Atlantic coast of North America
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: led to a decline in the population of eastern oysters in the region.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Dusky sharks do not typically consume eastern oysters
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: but do consume cownose rays, which are the main predators of the oysters.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: King Lear is a circa 1606 play by William Shakespeare.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: In the play, the character of King Lear attempts to test his three daughters’ devotion to him.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: He later expresses regret for his actions, as is evident when he ______
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: In the twentieth century, ethnographers made a concerted effort to collect Mexican American folklore, but they did not always agree about that folklore’s origins.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Scholars such as Aurelio Espinosa claimed that Mexican American folklore derived largely from the folklore of Spain, which ruled Mexico and what is now the southwestern United States from the sixteenth to early nineteenth centuries.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Scholars such as Américo Paredes, by contrast, argued that while some Spanish influence is undeniable, Mexican American folklore is mainly the product of the ongoing interactions of various cultures in Mexico and the United States.
sentence_analysis.label: Contrast

sentence_analysis.text: Perovskite solar cells convert light into electricity more efficiently than earlier kinds of solar cells, and manufacturing advances have recently made them commercially attractive.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: One limitation of the cells, however, has to do with their electron transport layer (ETL), through which absorbed electrons must pass.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: Often the ETL is applied through a process called spin coating, but such ETLs are fairly inefficient at converting input power to output power.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: André Taylor and colleagues tested a novel spray coating method for applying the ETL.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: The team produced ETLs of various thicknesses and concluded that spray coating holds promise for improving the power conversion efficiency of ETLs in perovskite solar cells.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Earth’s atmosphere is bombarded by cosmic dust originating from several sources: short-period comets (SPCs), particles from the asteroid belt (ASTs), Halley-type comets (HTCs), and Oort cloud comets (OCCs).
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Some of the dust’s material vaporizes in the atmosphere in a process called ablation, and the faster the particles move, the higher the rate of ablation.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Astrophysicist Juan Diego Carrillo-Sánchez led a team that calculated average ablation rates for elements in the dust (such as iron and potassium) and showed that material in slower-moving SPC or AST dust has a lower rate than the same material in faster-moving HTC or OCC dust.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: For example, whereas the average ablation rate for iron from AST dust is 28%, the average rate for ______
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: Native to Latin America, the cane toad was introduced to Australia in the 1930s.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: In recent decades, tadpoles in the Australian population have been shown to consume eggs of their own species.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: A 2022 study showed that when presented with cane toad eggs as well as eggs of native Australian amphibians, cane toad tadpoles disproportionately consumed eggs of their own species.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: This behavior results from their attraction to bufadienolide, a chemical produced by the eggs of cane toads but not by the eggs of native amphibians.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: However, using data from this study, a student wishes to argue that the presence of bufadienolide doesn’t entirely explain the cane toad tadpoles’ preference for certain eggs over others.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: In vertical inheritance, parents pass genes to their offspring, but in horizontal transfer (HT), one species, often bacteria, passes genetic material to an unrelated species.
sentence_analysis.label: Definition

sentence_analysis.text: In a 2022 study, herpetologist Atsushi Kurabayashi and his team investigated HT in multicellular organisms—namely, snakes and frogs in Madagascar.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The team detected BovB—a gene transmitted vertically in snakes—in many frog species.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: The apparent direction of gene transfer seems counterintuitive because frogs usually don’t survive encounters with snakes and so wouldn’t be able to transmit the newly acquired gene to offspring,
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: but the team concluded that BovB is indeed transmitted from snakes to frogs, either directly or indirectly, via HT.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Biologist Valentina Gómez-Bahamón and her team have investigated two subspecies of the fork-tailed flycatcher bird that live in the same region in Colombia, but one subspecies migrates south for part of the year, and the other doesn’t.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The researchers found that, due to slight differences in feather shape, the feathers of migratory forked-tailed flycatcher males make a sound during flight that is higher pitched than that made by the feathers of nonmigratory males.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: The researchers hypothesize that fork-tailed flycatcher females are attracted to the specific sound made by the males of their own subspecies, and that over time the females’ preference will drive further genetic and anatomical divergence between the subspecies.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: To study how floral damage affects the behavior of pollinators, such as bees, a team of researchers punched holes in the floral tissue of flowers from the vine yellow jessamine (Gelsemium sempervirens), a plant that produces flowers that have either a long pistil and a short stamen (pin morphs) or a short pistil and a long stamen (thrum morphs).
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The researchers then compared the time different insect pollinators spent visiting intact pin and thrum flowers to the time such pollinators spent visiting the artificially damaged pin and thrum flowers.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The researchers concluded that the effect of floral damage on time spent per flower varied by both floral morph and the genus of the pollinator.
sentence_analysis.label: Conclusion

sentence_analysis.text: “The Poet Walt Whitman” is an 1887 essay by José Martí, a Cuban author and political activist, originally written in Spanish.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: In the essay, Martí explores the value of literature, arguing that a society’s spiritual well-being depends on the character of its literary culture.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Aerial robots vary considerably in their holding force; the Ultra-Fast Robot Hand, for example, has a holding force of 56 newtons, more than twice that of the Permanent Magnet Hand and more than four times that of the Yale Model T.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: Since an aerial robot must lift its own weight along with its cargo, engineer Jiawei Meng and colleagues used a ratio of each robot’s holding force to the robot’s weight to calculate payload capacity, with higher ratios corresponding to greater capacity,
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: concluding that the Ultra-Fast Robot Hand has a higher payload capacity than the Yale Model T.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: “The Young Girl” is a 1920 short story by Katherine Mansfield.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: In the story, the narrator takes an unnamed seventeen-year-old girl and her younger brother out for a meal.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: In describing the teenager, Mansfield frequently contrasts the character’s pleasant appearance with her unpleasant attitude,
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: as when Mansfield writes of the teenager, ______
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: A student is writing a paper about One Night in Miami..., a 2020 film directed by Regina King and written by Kemp Powers.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Powers adapted the film’s screenplay from his 2013 play, which he wrote after learning about a 1964 meeting that took place in Miami, Florida, between four prominent figures of the Civil Rights movement: Malcolm X, Muhammad Ali, Jim Brown, and Sam Cooke.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The student claims that although Powers was inspired by this meeting, the film is best understood not as a precise retelling of historical events but rather as a largely imagined but informed representation of them.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), a band of clouds that encircles Earth in the tropics and is a major rainfall source, shifts position in response to temperature variations across Earth’s hemispheres.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Data from Huagapo Cave in Peru suggest the ITCZ shifted south during the Little Ice Age (circa 1300–1850), but a shift as far into South America as Huagapo should have led to dry conditions in Central America, which is inconsistent with climate models.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: To resolve the issue, geologist Yemane Asmerom and colleagues collected data from Yok Balum Cave in Central America and compared them with the Huagapo data.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: They concluded that during the Little Ice Age, the ITCZ may have expanded northward and southward rather than simply shifted.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: The largest tyrannosaurids—the family of carnivorous dinosaurs that includes Tarbosaurus, Albertosaurus, and, most famously, Tyrannosaurus rex—are thought to have had the strongest bites of any land animals in Earth’s history.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Paleontologists were excited to discover a second small fossil that is similar to the strange O. khaungraae fossil but has part of the lower body along with a birdlike skull.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: Detailed studies of both fossils revealed several traits that are found in lizards but not in dinosaurs or birds.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Therefore, paleontologists think the two creatures were probably unusual lizards, even though the skulls looked avian at first.
sentence_analysis.label: Conclusion

sentence_analysis.text: It seems clear that emotional contagion (the unintentional transfer of an emotional state from one person to another)
sentence_analysis.label: Definition

sentence_analysis.text: requires physical interaction and the observation of body language.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: After all, research shows that talking to someone who is smiling and expressing positive feelings often causes people to respond in a comparably positive way.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Similarly, displays of nervous fidgeting have been found to prompt others to begin behaving more nervously, too.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: In an experiment using a social networking service, Zeyao Yang and Emilio Ferrara found evidence of emotional contagion in text-based online interactions.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: The researchers discovered that reading social media posts that expressed a positive outlook led people to make more positive posts themselves, while posts with a negative emotional tone led people to make more negative posts.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Many studies in psychology have shown that people seek out information even when they know in advance that they have no immediate use for it and that they won’t directly benefit from it.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Such findings support the consensus view among researchers of curiosity: namely, that curiosity is not instrumental but instead represents a drive to acquire information for its own sake.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: While acknowledging that acquiring information is a powerful motivator, Rachit Dubey and colleagues ran an experiment to test whether emphasizing the usefulness of scientific information could increase curiosity about it.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: They found that when research involving rats and fruit flies was presented as having medical applications for humans, participants expressed greater interest in learning about it than when the research was not presented as useful.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: An excavation in Chiquihuite Cave in central Mexico has upended the belief that approximately 13,000 years ago, a group known as the Clovis people were the first human inhabitants of North America.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: More than 200 crude stone tools were found embedded in a layer of earth that is up to 33,150 years old, revealing that humans occupied the cave thousands of years before the Clovis people reached the continent.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: The objects uncovered in Chiquihuite Cave are intriguing, but it is premature to characterize them as tools.
sentence_analysis.label: Concession

sentence_analysis.text: The stone pieces are so roughly shaped that they may have simply fractured from rocks during natural geological activity in the cave.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: Moreover, their unearthing has thus far not been accompanied by discoveries of other signs of human activity or even traces of human DNA from surfaces.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: In 1954 George Balanchine choreographed a production of The Nutcracker, a ballet by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: It has since become a tradition for hundreds of dance companies in North America to stage The Nutcracker each year.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: But the show is stuck in the past, with an old-fashioned story and references, so it should no longer be produced.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Ballet needs to create new traditions if it wants to stay relevant to contemporary audiences.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The Nutcracker is outdated, but it should be kept because it’s a holiday favorite and provides substantial income for some dance companies.
sentence_analysis.label: Contrast

sentence_analysis.text: Although it can be behind the times, there are creative ways to update the show.
sentence_analysis.label: Concession

sentence_analysis.text: For example, Debbie Allen successfully modernized the story.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: Her show Hot Chocolate Nutcracker combines ballet, tap, hip-hop, and other styles, and it has been gaining in popularity since it opened in 2009.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Polar bears sustain themselves primarily by hunting seals on the Arctic sea ice, but rising ocean temperatures are causing the ice to diminish, raising concerns about polar bear population declines as these large predators’ seal-hunting habitats continue to shrink.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: A 2020 study examining polar bear populations across the Arctic concluded that populations affected by sea-ice loss are at great risk of extinction by the end of the twenty-first century.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Monitoring carried out by researchers from the Norwegian Polar Institute shows that the polar bear population on the Arctic archipelago of Svalbard remains stable and well nourished despite rapidly declining sea ice in recent years.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The researchers attribute this population’s resilience in part to a shift in feeding strategies: in addition to hunting seals, the Svalbard polar bears have begun relying on a diet of reindeer meat and birds’ eggs.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: A study by Dr. Paul Hanel and colleagues concluded that people are more likely to behave politely when listening to ideas they disagree with if they think about values before they engage in a discussion.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Study participants were assigned to one of two groups.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The experimental group spent a few minutes writing about one of their personal values before they had a group discussion on a controversial topic.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: And the control group spent a few minutes writing about a drink (tea, milk, etc.) before their group discussion on that topic.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: Hanel and colleagues found that the experimental group’s discussion was more civil than the control group’s discussion was.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Early in the Great Migration of 1910–1970, which involved the mass migration of Black people from the southern to the northern United States, political activist and Chicago Defender writer Fannie Barrier Williams was instrumental in helping other Black women establish themselves in the North.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Many women hoped for better employment opportunities in the North because, in the South, they faced much competition for domestic employment and men tended to get agricultural work.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: To aid with this transition, Barrier Williams helped secure job placement in the North for many women before they even began their journey.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: Archeological excavation of Market Street Chinatown, a nineteenth-century Chinese American community in San Jose, California, provided the first evidence that Asian food products were imported to the United States in the 1800s: bones from a freshwater fish species native to Southeast Asia.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Jinshanzhuang—Hong Kong–based import/export firms—likely coordinated the fish’s transport from Chinese-operated fisheries in Vietnam and Malaysia to North American markets.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: This route reveals the (often overlooked) multinational dimensions of the trade networks linking Chinese diaspora communities.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: In 1154, Muhammad al-Idrisi completed a collection of maps of the lands known to medieval Arabic and European scholars.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: This collection was titled Al-Kitāb al-Rujārī (The Book of Roger), after the Norman king Roger II who hired him to create it.
sentence_analysis.label: Definition

sentence_analysis.text: To create the collection, al-Idrisi consulted Arabic and Greek maps and interviewed travelers about the lands they visited.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: He included these travelers’ stories alongside the map illustrations.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: Using NASA’s powerful James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), Mercedes López-Morales and colleagues measured the wavelengths of light traveling through the atmosphere of WASP-39b, an exoplanet, or planet outside our solar system.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Different molecules absorb different wavelengths of light, and the wavelength measurements showed the presence of carbon dioxide (CO₂) in WASP-39b’s atmosphere.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: This finding not only offers the first decisive evidence of CO₂ in the atmosphere of an exoplanet but also illustrates the potential for future scientific breakthroughs held by the JWST.
sentence_analysis.label: Conclusion

sentence_analysis.text: Yawn contagion occurs when one individual yawns in response to another’s yawn.
sentence_analysis.label: Definition

sentence_analysis.text: Studies of this behavior in primates have focused on populations in captivity, but biologist Elisabetta Palagi and her colleagues have shown that it can occur in wild primate populations as well.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: In their study, which focused on a wild population of gelada monkeys (Theropithecus gelada) in Ethiopia, the researchers further reported that yawn contagion most commonly occurred in males and across different social groups instead of within a single social group.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: On painter William H. Johnson’s return to the United States in 1938 after a decade in Europe, his style underwent an abrupt transformation.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Turning away from landscapes painted in an expressionist style—a style that often involves using fluid, distorted shapes and thick, textured brushstrokes to express the artist’s subjective experience of reality—Johnson began painting portraits of Black Americans in a bold new way.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Evocative of African sculpture and American and Scandinavian folk art, these portraits feature flat, deliberately oversimplified figures in a vibrant but limited color palette.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: Very little is known about the role nocturnal insects, such as moths, play in flower pollination because it is difficult to monitor insects at night.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: To address this problem, a team of scientists used time-lapse cameras to record pollinator visits to red clover all day and night.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: The recordings showed that while most pollinator visits were by bumblebees, one-third of visits were by moths.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Additionally, flowers that were visited by both moths and bees produced more seeds than flowers that were only visited by bees.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: Chile’s Atacama Desert is one of the driest places on Earth.

sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The algae and bacteria found in Atacama’s driest regions may offer clues about Martian life.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: By studying how these and other microorganisms survive such extreme conditions on Earth, Wilhelm’s team hopes to determine whether similar life might have existed on Mars and to develop the best tools to look for evidence of it.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: Researchers have long hypothesized that woolly mammoths were hunted to extinction in North America by humans using spears with grooved tips known as Clovis points.

sentence_analysis.text: One anthropologist set out to test this hypothesis.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Using a mechanical spear-thrower, he launched spears with Clovis points into mounds of clay—substitutes for the animals’ large bodies.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: The projectiles generally penetrated only a few inches into the clay, an amount insufficient to have harmed most woolly mammoths.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: This led the anthropologist to conclude that hunters using spears with Clovis points likely weren’t the principal drivers of the extinction.
sentence_analysis.label: Conclusion

sentence_analysis.text: When ancient oak planks were unearthed during subway construction in Rome, Mauro Bernabei and his team examined the growth rings in the wood to determine where these planks came from.

sentence_analysis.text: By comparing the growth rings on the planks to records of similar rings in oaks from Europe, the team could trace the wood to the Jura region of France, hundreds of kilometers from Rome.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Because timber could only have been transported from distant Jura to Rome by boat, the team’s findings suggest the complexity of Roman trade routes.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Meteorites found on Earth are divided into two categories.

sentence_analysis.text: A meteorite that was observed falling to Earth before being recovered is known as a meteorite fall.

sentence_analysis.text: All other meteorites found on Earth are known as meteorite finds.

sentence_analysis.text: There have been about 1,200 recorded meteorite falls.

sentence_analysis.text: In astronomy, the mass of stars can be described in units called solar masses.

sentence_analysis.text: Pterosaurs were flying reptiles that existed millions of years ago.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: In a 2021 study, Anusuya Chinsamy-Turan analyzed fragments of pterosaur jawbones located in the Sahara Desert.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: She was initially unsure if the bones belonged to juvenile or adult pterosaurs.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: She used advanced microscope techniques to determine that the bones had few growth lines relative to the bones of fully grown pterosaurs.

sentence_analysis.text: Some US reformers sought to improve society in the 1800s by building utopias.

sentence_analysis.text: In 1999, astronomer Todd Henry studied the differences in surface temperature between the Sun and nearby stars.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: His team mapped all stars within 10 parsecs (approximately 200 trillion miles) of the Sun.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: The surface temperature of the Sun is around 9,800°F, which classifies it as a G star.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: 327 of the 357 stars in the study were classified as K or M stars, with surface temperatures under 8,900°F (cooler than the Sun).
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: 11 of the 357 stars in the study were classified as A or F stars, with surface temperatures greater than 10,300°F (hotter than the Sun).

sentence_analysis.text: Elizabeth Catlett’s sculpture Recognition (1970) shows two African American figures with rounded, indistinct features.
