sentence_analysis.text: As carbon levels increase, the audio is correspondingly distorted; ______ listeners can 'hear' the changes in the carbon levels.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Archaeologist Sue Brunning explains why the seventh-century ship burial site at Sutton Hoo in England was likely the tomb of a king.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: First, the gold artifacts inside the ship suggest that the person buried with them was a wealthy and respected leader.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: ______ the massive effort required to bury the ship would likely only have been undertaken for a king.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: In the early 1900s, Jovita Idár fought injustice on both sides of the Mexico–United States border.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: As a reporter for the Texas newspaper La Crónica, she voiced support for the Mexican people’s revolt against authoritarian rule.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: ______ she founded the League of Mexican Women, a group that advocated for the rights of Mexican Americans.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: In November 1934, Amrita Sher-Gil was living in what must have seemed like the ideal city for a young artist: Paris.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: She was studying firsthand the color-saturated style of France’s modernist masters and beginning to make a name for herself as a painter.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Sher-Gil longed to return to her childhood home of India; only there, she believed, could her art truly flourish.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Mary Ellen Pleasant, a successful entrepreneur during the gold rush era, earned the moniker 'Mother of Human Rights in California' after successfully challenging discrimination in the state.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: In 1866, she sued a streetcar company for denying her and other Black riders service, a suit she eventually won when the California Supreme Court declared it illegal for carriers to exclude passengers based on race.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: “Wishcycling”—putting nonrecyclable items into recycling bins under the mistaken belief that those items can be recycled—ultimately does more harm than good.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Nonrecyclable items, such as greasy pizza boxes, can contaminate recyclable materials, rendering entire batches unusable.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: ______ nonrecyclable products can damage recycling plants’ machinery.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: At two weeks old, the time their critical socialization period begins, wolves can smell but cannot yet see or hear.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Domesticated dogs, ______ can see, hear, and smell by the end of two weeks.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: This relative lack of sensory input may help explain why wolves behave so differently around humans than dogs do: from a very young age, wolves are more wary and less exploratory.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: To discover which fruit varieties were grown in Italy’s Umbria region before the introduction of industrial farming, botanist Isabella Dalla Ragione often turns to centuries-old lists of cooking ingredients.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: she analyzes Renaissance paintings of Umbria, as they can provide accurate representations of fruits that were grown there long ago.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: A common assumption among art historians is that the invention of photography in the mid-nineteenth century displaced the painted portrait in the public consciousness.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The diminishing popularity of the portrait miniature, which coincided with the rise of photography, seems to support this claim.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: However, photography’s impact on the portrait miniature may be overstated.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Although records from art exhibitions in the Netherlands from 1820 to 1892 show a decrease in the number of both full-sized and miniature portraits submitted, this trend was established before the invention of photography.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Believing that living in an impractical space can heighten awareness and even improve health, conceptual artists Madeline Gins and Shusaku Arakawa designed an apartment building in Japan to be more fanciful than functional.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: A kitchen counter is chest-high on one side and knee-high on the other; a ceiling has a door to nowhere.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: The effect is disorienting but invigorating: after four years there, filmmaker Nobu Yamaoka reported significant health benefits.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: During the World War II era, some Mexican American women adopted a striking new look called pachuca style.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: They wore altered men’s jackets or zoot suits (wide-legged, long-coated suits) and dramatic makeup, and they combed their hair into high, rounded shapes.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: Some people criticized pachuca style, saying it was dangerous and women should dress traditionally.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: But historians see things differently.
sentence_analysis.label: Contrast

sentence_analysis.text: They see pachuca style as a form of rebellion against the era’s rigid social expectations for women.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: They say that it showed a desire for self-expression and freedom on the part of women who adopted the style.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: Utah is home to Pando, a colony of about 47,000 quaking aspen trees that all share a single root system.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Pando is one of the largest single organisms by mass on Earth, but ecologists are worried that its growth is declining in part because of grazing by animals.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The ecologists say that strong fences could prevent deer from eating young trees and help Pando start thriving again.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: Biologists have predicted that birds’ feather structures vary with habitat temperature, but this hadn’t been tested in mountain environments.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Ornithologist Sahas Barve studied feathers from 249 songbird species inhabiting different elevations—and thus experiencing different temperatures—in the Himalaya Mountains.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: He found that feathers of high-elevation species not only have a greater proportion of warming downy sections to flat and smooth sections than do feathers of low-elevation species, but high-elevation species’ feathers also tend to be longer, providing a thicker layer of insulation.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Paleontologists searching for signs of ancient life have found many fossilized specimens of prehistoric human ancestors, including several from the Pleistocene era discovered in a geological formation in the Minatogawa quarry in Japan.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: However, to study the emergence of the earliest multicellular organisms to appear on Earth, researchers must turn elsewhere, such as to the Ediacaran geological formation at Mistaken Point in Canada.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: A UNESCO World Heritage Site, the 146-hectare reserve contains more than 10,000 fossils that together document a critical moment in evolutionary history.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: The following text is adapted from Edgar Allan Poe’s 1849 story “Landor’s Cottage.”
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: During a pedestrian trip last summer, through one or two of the river counties of New York, I found myself, as the day declined, somewhat embarrassed about the road I was pursuing.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The land undulated very remarkably; and my path, for the last hour, had wound about and about so confusedly, in its effort to keep in the valleys, that I no longer knew in what direction lay the sweet village of B——, where I had determined to stop for the night.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: A contraction of “you all,” the pronoun “y’all” has long been used as a plural version of “you” in the South and in Black communities around the US.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: In recent decades, most other English-speaking communities in the US have begun to use “y’all.”
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: What explains its rise in popularity?
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: Many varieties of English have no pronoun that specifically addresses more than one person and instead must use “you” to address both one person and more than one.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: But “y’all” always refers to two or more people.
sentence_analysis.label: Contrast

sentence_analysis.text: As a result, it conveys the speaker’s meaning more precisely than “you” can.
sentence_analysis.label: Conclusion

sentence_analysis.text: In 1934 physicist Eugene Wigner posited the existence of a crystal consisting entirely of electrons in a honeycomb-like structure.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The so-called Wigner crystal remained largely conjecture, however, until Feng Wang and colleagues announced in 2021 that they had captured an image of one.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The researchers trapped electrons between two semiconductors and then cooled the apparatus, causing the electrons to settle into a crystalline structure.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: By inserting an ultrathin sheet of graphene above the crystal, the researchers obtained an impression—the first visual confirmation of the Wigner crystal.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Paleontologist Alan Tennyson and colleagues studied fossil bones found in New Zealand that are more than 55 million years old.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The researchers determined that the fossil bones belonged to two previously unknown species of prehistoric penguins.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Moreover, they estimated that one of the two penguin species was more than three times the size of the emperor penguin, which is the largest penguin species that exists today.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Philadelphia’s Black Pearl Chamber Orchestra, founded by Jeri Lynne Johnson, performs classical music, from well-known compositions by Beethoven to contemporary works by Jessie Montgomery.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: For the orchestra’s iConduct! program, Johnson invites community members to learn some basic elements of conducting and then experience conducting the Black Pearl orchestra themselves.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: In West Africa, jalis have traditionally been keepers of information about family histories and records of important events.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: They have often served as teachers and advisers, too.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: New technologies may have changed some aspects of the role today, but jalis continue to be valued for knowing and protecting their peoples’ stories.
sentence_analysis.label: Contrast

sentence_analysis.text: The following text is from Anton Chekhov’s 1898 short story “Ionitch” (translated by Marian Fell in 1915).
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The text is set in a Russian city referred to as the city of S.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: If newcomers to the little provincial city of S. complained that life there was monotonous and dull, its inhabitants would answer that, on the contrary, S. was a very amusing place, indeed, that it had a library and a club, that balls were given there, and finally, that very pleasant families lived there with whom one might become acquainted.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: And they always pointed to the Turkins as the most accomplished and most enlightened family of all.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: To dye wool, Navajo (Diné) weaver Lillie Taylor uses plants and vegetables from Arizona, where she lives.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: For example, she achieved the deep reds and browns featured in her 2003 rug In the Path of the Four Seasons by using Arizona dock roots, drying and grinding them before mixing the powder with water to create a dye bath.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: To intensify the appearance of certain colors, Taylor also sometimes mixes in clay obtained from nearby soil.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: The ancient writing system used in the Maya kingdoms of southern Mexico and Central America had a symbol for the number zero.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The earliest known example of the symbol dates to more than 2,000 years ago.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: At that time, almost none of the writing systems elsewhere in the world possessed a zero symbol.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: And the use of zero in Mexico and Central America may be even more ancient.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Some historians suggest that Maya mathematicians inherited it from the Olmec civilization, which flourished in the region 2,400–3,600 years ago.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: In present-day Chiapas, Mexico, archaeologist Robert Rosenswig, remote-sensing specialist Ricardo López-Torrijos, and colleagues have located 41 smaller settlements surrounding the ancient Mesoamerican city of Izapa.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The researchers have concluded that these settlements were culturally linked to Izapa because each of the settlements is the same age and configured in the same manner as Izapa, with a pyramid to the north and a plaza to the south.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Their shared structural orientation suggests that residents of the settlements likely performed some of the same cultural ceremonies as residents in Izapa did.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: The painter María Izquierdo played an important role in the development of twentieth-century Mexican art, but her work has never been well-known in the United States except among art historians.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: One reason for Izquierdo’s relative obscurity is the enormous popularity of some of her peers.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: In particular, the painters Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera have so captivated the interest of US audiences that Izquierdo and other Mexican artists from the period often get overlooked, despite the high quality of their work.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Since its completion in 2014, Bosco Verticale (Vertical Forest)—a pair of residential towers in Milan, Italy, covered by vegetation—has become a striking symbol of environmental sustainability in architecture.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Stefano Boeri intended his design, which features balconies that are home to hundreds of trees, to serve as a model for promoting urban biodiversity.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: However, the concept has faced skepticism: critics note that although the trees used in Bosco Verticale were specifically cultivated for the project, it’s too early to tell if they can thrive in this unusual setting.
sentence_analysis.label: Contrast

sentence_analysis.text: Choctaw/Cherokee artist Jeffrey Gibson turns punching bags used by boxers into art by decorating them with beadwork and elements of Native dressmaking.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: These elements include leather fringe and jingles, the metal cones that cover the dresses worn in the jingle dance, a women’s dance of the Ojibwe people.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: Thus, Gibson combines an object commonly associated with masculinity (a punching bag) with art forms traditionally practiced by women in most Native communities (beadwork and dressmaking).
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: In this way, he rejects the division of male and female gender roles.
sentence_analysis.label: Conclusion

sentence_analysis.text: The following text is from Ahmet Hamdi Tanpinar’s 1961 novel The Time Regulation Institute (translated from the Turkish in 2014 by Maureen Freely and Alexander Dawe).
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The narrator was once involved with the Time Regulation Institute, a fictional bureaucracy that regulates the time of Turkey’s clocks.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: I may be the most humble and absurd man in the world and, as my wife says, the most slovenly creature you may ever meet—that is, before the founding of our institute—but I did come to know a truly great man who possessed a natural genius for invention.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: I spent years at his side.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: I watched the way he worked.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: I witnessed how an idea would suddenly catch fire in his mind and take shape, like a tree sprouting shoots and branches, before coming into being.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: A subject of much speculation, distinctive sets of parallel ridges mark the icy crust of Europa, Jupiter’s smallest moon.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Researchers now claim that the ridges’ formation mechanism mirrors that of a strikingly similar pair on Greenland’s ice sheet.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: There, surface water seeped through fissures in the sheet and formed a water pocket that subsequently disrupted the overlying ice, forcing fragments of it upward and outward into peaks, as the pocket froze and expanded.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: Although Europa lacks liquid surface water, the same process could be driven by the moon’s subsurface ocean.
sentence_analysis.label: Concession

sentence_analysis.text: NASA’s Aspera mission, led by Carlos Vargas, will investigate the circumgalactic medium (CGM), the huge swaths of low-density gas that fill and surround galaxies.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Specifically, the team will focus on portions of the gas that exist in a 'warm-hot' phase: these portions haven’t previously been observable but are thought to fuel new star formation and hold most of the mass that makes up a galaxy.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Using a telescope capable of revealing these parts of the CGM, the Aspera mission should help answer long-standing questions about how galaxies emerge, change, and even interact.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: Many intellectual histories of the Black Power movement of the 1960s and 1970s rely heavily on essays and other explicitly ideological works as primary sources, a tendency that can overrepresent the perspectives of a small number of thinkers, most of whom were male.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Historian Ashley D. Farmer has shown that expanding the array of primary sources to encompass more types of print material—including political cartoons, advertisements, and artwork—leads to a much better understanding of the movement and the crucial and diverse roles that Black women played in shaping it.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Using the Stratospheric Observatory for Infrared Astronomy (SOFIA), a team of astronomers mapped out the magnetic field of G47, one of the Milky Way’s galactic bones (dense clouds of gas and dust that run through the middle of the arm of a spiral galaxy).
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Surprisingly, the map revealed a magnetic field with no clear pattern or direction.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: The researchers had expected the magnetic field to be similar to the more uniform fields seen in galactic bones in other arms of the Milky Way.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: In many of his sculptures, artist Richard Hunt uses broad forms rather than extreme accuracy to hint at specific people or ideas.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: In his first major work, Arachne (1956), Hunt constructed the mythical character Arachne, a weaver who was changed into a spider, by welding bits of steel together into something that, although vaguely human, is strange and machine-like.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: And his large bronze sculpture The Light of Truth (2021) commemorates activist and journalist Ida B. Wells using mainly flowing, curved pieces of metal that create stylized flame.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: The following text is adapted from Robert Louis Stevenson’s 1883 novel Treasure Island.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Bill is a sailor staying at the Admiral Benbow, an inn run by the narrator’s parents.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Every day when [Bill] came back from his stroll he would ask if any seafaring men had gone by along the road.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: At first we thought it was the want of company of his own kind that made him ask this question, but at last we began to see he was desirous to avoid them.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: When a seaman did [stay] at the Admiral Benbow (as now and then some did) he would look in at him through the curtained door before he entered the parlour;
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: and he was always sure to be as silent as a mouse when any such was present.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: The following text is adapted from Guy de Maupassant’s nineteenth-century short story “The Trip of Le Horla” (translated by Albert M. C. McMaster, A. E. Henderson, Mme. Quesada, et al.).
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The narrator is part of a group traveling in a hot-air balloon at night.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The earth no longer seems to exist, it is buried in milky vapors that resemble a sea.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: We are now alone in space with the moon, which looks like another balloon travelling opposite us;
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: and our balloon, which shines in the air, appears like another, larger moon, a world wandering in the sky amid the stars, through infinity.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: We no longer speak, think nor live; we float along through space in delicious inertia.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The air which is bearing us up has made of us all beings which resemble itself, silent, joyous, irresponsible beings, peculiarly alert, although motionless.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: The recovery of a 1,000-year-old Chinese shipwreck in the Java Sea near present-day Indonesia has yielded a treasure trove of artifacts, including thousands of small ceramic bowls.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Using a portable X-ray fluorescence analyzer tool, Lisa Niziolek and her team were able to detect the chemical composition of these bowls without damaging them.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: By comparing the chemical signatures of the bowls with those of the materials still at old Chinese kiln sites, Niziolek and her team can pinpoint which Chinese kilns likely produced the ceramic bowls.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: I wish I could remember that first day, First hour, first moment of your meeting me,
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: If bright or dim the season, it might be Summer or Winter for [all] I can say; So unrecorded did it slip away,
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: So blind was I to see and to foresee,
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: So dull to mark the budding of my tree
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: That would not blossom yet for many a May.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Archaeologists have discovered a runestone in Norway that may contain the earliest example of written words in Scandinavia.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Carbon dating at the discovery site revealed that the stone was likely carved between 1 and 250 CE.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Runologist Kristel Zilmer believes the stone will be helpful in learning more about the use of runic alphabets in early Iron Age Scandinavia.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The following text is from Ezra Pound’s 1909 poem “Hymn III,” based on the work of Marcantonio Flaminio.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: As a fragile and lovely flower unfolds its gleaming foliage on the breast of the fostering earth, if the dew and the rain draw it forth;
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: So doth my tender mind flourish, if it be fed with the sweet dew of the fostering spirit,
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Lacking this, it beginneth straightway to languish,
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: even as a floweret born upon dry earth, if the dew and the rain tend it not.
sentence_analysis.label: Example

sentence_analysis.text: To understand how Paleolithic artists navigated dark caves, archaeologist Mª Ángeles Medina-Alcaide and her team tested different lighting methods in a cave in Spain using replicas of artifacts found in European caves with art.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: They used three different Paleolithic light sources—torches, animal-fat lamps, and fireplaces—determining that each likely had a specific purpose.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: For instance, the team learned that the animal-fat lamps were less useful than torches while walking because the lamps didn’t illuminate the cave floor.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Microplastics are tiny pieces of plastic waste.
sentence_analysis.label: Definition

sentence_analysis.text: Areas of the ocean with higher concentrations of microplastic particles also have smaller and fewer waves.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: A study by Yukun Sun and colleagues found that the concentration of microplastic particles cannot be the only reason for this reduced wave activity because the concentration of particles that would have the observed effect is much higher than that found in these areas of the ocean.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: However, they found that surfactants, chemicals often used to manufacture plastics, are released into the water from microplastics and have a much stronger wave-reducing effect.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: The ice melted on a Norwegian mountain during a particularly warm summer in 2019, revealing a 1,700-year-old sandal to a mountaineer looking for artifacts.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The sandal would normally have degraded quickly, but it was instead well preserved for centuries by the surrounding ice.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The following text is adapted from Jack London’s 1903 novel The Call of the Wild.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Buck is a sled dog living with John Thornton in Yukon, Canada.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Thornton alone held [Buck].
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The rest of mankind was as nothing.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Chance travellers might praise or pet him; but he was cold under it all, and from a too demonstrative man he would get up and walk away.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: When Thornton’s partners, Hans and Pete, arrived on the long-expected raft, Buck refused to notice them till he learned they were close to Thornton;
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: after that he tolerated them in a passive sort of way, accepting favors from them as though he favored them by accepting.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: To protect themselves when being attacked, hagfish—jawless marine animals that resemble eels—will release large quantities of slimy, mucus-like threads.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Because these threads are unusually strong and elastic, scientist Atsuko Negishi and her colleagues have been trying to recreate them in a lab as an eco-friendly alternative to petroleum-based fibers that are often used in fabrics.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The researchers want to reproduce the threads in the lab because farming hagfish for their slime would be expensive and potentially harmful to the hagfish.
sentence_analysis.label: Problem

sentence_analysis.text: Culinary anthropologist Vertamae Smart-Grosvenor may be known for her decades of work in national public television and radio, but her book Vibration Cooking: or, the Travel Notes of a Geechee Girl is likely her most influential project.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: The 1970 book, whose title refers to Smart-Grosvenor’s roots in the Low Country of South Carolina, was unusual for its time.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: It combined memoir, recipes, travel writing, and social commentary and challenged notions about conventions of food and cooking.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Long admired by many, the book and its author have shaped contemporary approaches to writing about cuisine.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: Recently, scientists looked at data collected by NASA’s InSight lander to learn more about seismic activity on Mars, known as marsquakes.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: The data show that the marsquakes all started from the same location on the planet.
sentence_analysis.label: Finding

sentence_analysis.text: This discovery was surprising to scientists, as they expected that the marsquakes would originate from all over the planet because of the cooling of the planet’s surface.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Now, scientists believe that there could be areas of active magma flows deep beneath the planet’s surface that trigger the marsquakes.
sentence_analysis.label: Solution

sentence_analysis.text: In her 1998 book Blues Legacies and Black Feminism, Angela Y. Davis bases her analysis in part on recordings of songs
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: sung in the 1920s by Gertrude “Ma” Rainey and Bessie Smith.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: Davis focuses on how Rainey and Smith improvised the lyrics—replacing the original lines with mischievous jokes and wordplay.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Davis’s work was particularly labor intensive because in order to transcribe, or write down, the lyrics as Rainey and Smith sang them, Davis had to listen repeatedly to the vinyl recordings, which weren’t very clear.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence

sentence_analysis.text: Mrs. Ochiltree was a woman of strong individuality, whose comments upon her acquaintance[s], present or absent, were marked by a frankness at times no less than startling.
sentence_analysis.label: Background

sentence_analysis.text: This characteristic caused her to be more or less avoided.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Mrs. Ochiltree was aware of this sentiment on the part of her acquaintance[s], and rather exulted in it.
sentence_analysis.label: Elaboration

sentence_analysis.text: Cats can judge unseen people’s positions in space by the sound of their voices and thus react with surprise when the same person calls to them from two different locations in a short span of time.
sentence_analysis.label: Claim

sentence_analysis.text: Saho Takagi and colleagues reached this conclusion by measuring cats’ levels of surprise based on their ear and head movements while the cats heard recordings of their owners’ voices from two speakers spaced far apart.
sentence_analysis.label: Evidence
